### [756b2a8](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/756b2a8b9e5fe1ef94023a2e8c304ee484e26288)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T08:37:38Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det_train): split count from the merge-resident limit for few-unit calls on sm_100a and sm_103a (#9081)

Cake ships two variants of its deterministic DSA indexer top-k training
kernel (`cake_dsa_indexer_det_train_topk`) in FlashInfer: the default
BF16 form and the opt-in FP8 (e4m3) form. Each form has a
sampled-threshold mode and a sampling-off mode, and the family ships on
sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a. This PR changes only BF16 split calls on
sm_100a and sm_103a. On these calls, the split count now comes from the
merge-resident limit (new policy field `split_resident_rule`), so the
split count changes on calls with few work units (mostly to more
splits), and the scan and merge programs stay the same. The baseline is
the previous Cake version, FlashInfer main `5dbf6b8a`, and speedup is
main time divided by this PR time. This PR was timed as commit
`1909735c` on that main. The PR commit `85656183` carries the same
change on main `d227d0eb`. The baseline `5dbf6b8a` predates #9019,
#9021, #9047 and #9052, which changed some scan programs (for example
the GB300 sampling-off `wide` rows), so the main ms of those same-plan
rows do not reflect current main; this PR's split counts are the same on
both mains. The timed set is the 32 prepared calls (sampling on and
off), the eager entry (8 calls), 8 split sweep calls and 94 split-count
calls. The split count changes on 83 timed shapes on GB300 and 80 on
GB200 and B200. W64_42k_k512, W64_42k_k4096 and W64_64k_k4096 change
only on sm_103a. On those shapes this PR runs 1.020x to 2.755x faster on
GB300, 1.021x to 2.642x on GB200 and 1.028x to 2.757x on B200. The
largest gain is W16_12k_k512, where the split count goes from 2 to 24.
Every other timed call runs the same program on both sides and falls
between 0.934x and 1.024x.

- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det_train): split calls fuse the slab rank finalize into the merge (#9078)

Cake ships two variants of its deterministic DSA indexer top-k training
kernel (`cake_dsa_indexer_det_train_topk`) in FlashInfer: the default
BF16 form and the opt-in FP8 (e4m3) form. Each form has a
sampled-threshold mode and a sampling-off mode, and the family ships on
sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a. This PR changes only BF16 split calls,
which are calls whose plan splits the key range over several CTAs and
then merges the partial candidates. On these calls, the final merge pass
now also writes the ranked output. This adds nine new `merge_rank` merge
programs and removes the separate rank finalize launch. The scan
programs, the split counts and every FP8 plan are unchanged. The
baseline is the previous Cake version, FlashInfer main `2eb2e8cb`, and
speedup is main time divided by this PR time. The 11 timed split shapes
get faster on every GPU: 1.050x to 1.125x on GB300, 1.056x to 1.122x on
GB200, 1.052x to 1.106x on B200 and 1.059x to 1.124x on sm_107a. Every
other timed call runs the same programs on both sides and falls between
0.968x and 1.038x. Those calls are in the folded tables. In the summary,
/s, /n and /e mark sampling on, sampling off and eager. The baseline
`2eb2e8cb` predates #9019, #9021, #9047 and #9052. Those PRs changed
some non-split programs, for example the GB300 sampling-off `wide` rows
and some sm_107a rows. As a result, the main ms in the folded tables do
not reflect current main. The split calls use `split_l6` /
`split_narrow`, which those PRs do not touch. The plan also changes for
16 further W/G split shapes (W1_64k, W4_64k, W16_64k, W64_32k, W64_64k,
W256_16k, W256_32k, W256_64k, G64x32k_s1, G64x64k_s1, G256x16k_s1,
G256x32k_s1, G256x64k_s1, G64x16k_s2, G64x32k_s2, G64x16k_s4), which
were not timed. GB300 and GB200 timed `ec796aec`. B200 and sm_107a timed
its parent `ae7d71bd`, which differs only in tests. The repeat timings
noted under the B200 and sm_107a tables ran `ec796aec`.

### [2f74b00](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2f74b00a8894894fcf1982b56f299f31eb74aa75)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T08:13:44Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda_det_kcp): run the forward's summary pair on two streams when K1 fills a wave (#9072)

`flashinfer.cake_kda_det_train_kcp` holds the deterministic
context-parallel (KCP) training kernels of KDA (Kimi Delta Attention).
In the forward, the summary pair is K1 (the offset walk from zero) and
K3 (the transfer walk over the same walk list). The pair also runs in
the replay forward of a replay-mode backward and in a checkpoint
recompute. Both kernels read the same operands and write disjoint tiles.
Neither reads the other's output, and only the next launch uses their
results. This PR issues K3 on a per-device side stream beside K1. A fork
event and a join event make every later launch, including the
collective, run after both. The PR uses two streams only when K1 alone
fills a wave of its two-CTA-per-SM slots, i.e. (walk segments × heads) ≥
2 × SM count. Below that it keeps one stream, and the launch sequence is
unchanged from main. On all three GPUs, H = 64 uses two streams on the
interior ranks and H = 16 keeps one. The kernels and the build are
unchanged. Outputs and every input gradient are bitwise identical to
main, and main is the baseline for all numbers below.

| H, mode | GB300 (sm_103a) | GB200 (sm_100a) | R200 (sm_107a) |
|---|---|---|---|
| H = 64, fwd | 2.7338 → 2.6990 (1.0129x) | 2.8568 → 2.8343 (1.0079x) |
1.6744 → 1.6410 (1.0204x) |
| H = 64, fwd+bwd | 7.9794 → 7.9478 (1.0040x) | 8.2799 → 8.2569
(1.0028x) | 5.2627 → 5.2295 (1.0063x) |
| H = 64, checkpointed fwd+bwd | 10.0073 → 9.9741 (1.0033x) | 10.4111 →
10.3929 (1.0018x) | 6.6544 → 6.6228 (1.0048x) |
| H = 16, fwd | 1.6945 → 1.6917 (1.0016x) | 1.7226 → 1.7297 (0.9959x) |
not timed |
| H = 16, fwd+bwd | 3.7062 → 3.7327 (0.9929x) | 3.7847 → 3.7841
(1.0002x) | not timed |
| H = 16, checkpointed fwd+bwd | 5.2651 → 5.3074 (0.9920x) | 5.3173 →
5.3317 (0.9973x) | not timed |

Values in ms, main → this PR (speedup = main / this PR). **Workload:**
CP4 (4 ranks), 65536 tokens in 4 documents (24576, 16384, 14336, 10240),
16384 tokens per rank with per-document zigzag, head dim K = V = 128, H
= 64 or 16 heads (Q/K and V). Inputs are BF16 q/k/v and beta, with FP32
per-channel gates and FP32 state. Q/K L2 norm runs in the kernel, with
no initial or final state. **Modes:** fwd, fwd+bwd, and checkpointed
fwd+bwd (torch.utils.checkpoint: forward, recompute, backward). **GB300
and GB200:** on each node the runs alternate main, this PR, this PR,
main, with 12 seeds × 20 iterations per visit. Step time is the max over
the 4 ranks, and each value is the median of 480 iterations per side.
**R200 (212 SMs):** this board shifts the whole step time between
processes. So main's launch sequence is compared with this PR's inside
the same process, because this PR with the side stream turned off issues
exactly main's launch sequence. The setup is 4 processes × 2 seeds × 12
alternating blocks, and the values are medians of the 4 per-process
medians. The paired change is −31.0 / −29.9 / −29.8 µs (fwd / fwd+bwd /
checkpointed), with bootstrap 95% intervals [−41.0, −24.6], [−33.5,
−26.8] and [−33.1, −23.2]. **H = 16:** the rule keeps one stream, so the
kernel launches equal main's. The GB300 and GB200 H = 16 values are
means over 4 (GB300) and 2 (GB200) alternating main/PR blocks. Per-block
changes on GB300 are fwd +10.8, −10.7, −20.1, +9.0 µs; fwd+bwd +37.4,
+11.0, −8.3, +66.0 µs; checkpointed +63.1, +24.0, −12.8, +95.1 µs. On
GB200 they are fwd +10.1, +4.0 µs; fwd+bwd +28.9, −30.2 µs; checkpointed
+50.2, −21.4 µs. A control block with main on both sides moved by up to
17.6 µs on GB300 and 18.9 µs on GB200. On GB300 at H = 16, a
same-process comparison of this PR's host path against main's gives this
PR minus main of +1.2 µs [−3.6, +4.0] (fwd), −2.8 µs [−12.0, +7.6]
(fwd+bwd) and +8.1 µs [−1.1, +21.7] (checkpointed). Every interval
includes zero. R200 at H = 16 is not timed because the rule keeps one
stream there (256 < 2 × 212), so the launches equal main's.
**Environment:** CUDA 13.4 (nvcc 13.4.92), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.

The other Cake variants of this kernel are the non-deterministic KCP
package `flashinfer.cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp` and the single-rank
packages `flashinfer.cake_kda_det_train` and
`flashinfer.cake_kda_nondet_train`, and the family ships on sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [c1cebf8](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c1cebf81ec84a6f64f6d6844d06e106ff5f56ad8)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T07:38:35Z
- **提交信息**: docs(training_backend_names): allow a KCP route inside its single-rank backend package (#9082)

## Summary

`docs/training_backend_names.md` rule 1 says every backend package sits
at `flashinfer/experimental/cake/<module>/`. The causal conv1d KCP route
does not follow it: its backend lives as `kcp.py` / `kcp_jit.py` inside
`cake_causal_conv1d_<mode>_train`.

This PR documents that layout as an exception instead of moving the
code:

- The KCP route runs the single-rank convolution programs and adds only
a halo exchange.
- A separate `cake_causal_conv1d_<mode>_train_kcp` backend package would
have to copy those programs or import across packages. Rule 1 and the
standalone-build layout forbid both.
- The `_kcp` facades stay at the top level and import the submodule
lazily, so public names do not change.

Changes:
- Rule 1: add the exception and its conditions.
- Decisions: record that causal conv1d KCP stays inside the single-rank
backend packages.

Docs only; no code changes.

Refs #8928

### [c556746](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c556746c3f6cb948367067e53b8eb37baf2c209b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T07:27:21Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): sm_103a FP8 paged-context one-stage form programs (#9073)

Cake's FP8 paged-context attention (FP8 Q/K/V, head dim 128) ships AOT
runtime-size programs at GQA packs 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12 and 16. It
has six forms. One is plain causal. The other five are flag forms: NC
(non-causal), LSE (causal with LSE output), SINK (causal with sinks),
NC_LSE and NC_SINK.

On sm_103a (GB300), the flag forms run `RUNTIME_PACK<p>_<FORM>_PX`
programs. These programs use a 4-stage K/V ring, a swapped P tile and
two Q stages, and shipped in a previous PR. The plain causal form
already has a one-Q-stage variant, `_PX_Q1`, for short query tiles.

This PR adds 20 sm_103a programs, `RUNTIME_PACK<p>_<FORM>_PX_Q1`, for
the five flag forms at packs 1, 2, 4 and 8. They keep the 4-stage ring
and swapped P tile but use one Q stage. On sm_103a, some flag-form calls
at packs 1, 2, 4 and 8 now take the `_PX_Q1` program. A call is routed
there when its query tile fits one stage (at most 128 query rows per
tile after GQA packing) and it has more than 128 keys. Other calls are
unchanged, and sm_100a (B200) is unchanged. The arithmetic does not
change. O and LSE are bitwise equal to the previous program and to the
JIT module.

The 45 routed rows run 1.149x to 1.253x faster than the previous
program. They are faster in each of the 10 memory layouts. No row is
slower.

**GB300 (sm_103a), CUDA 13.4. GPU time with cold L2 (CUPTI), median over
10 seeded memory layouts x 2 rounds.**

### [118aa08](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/118aa08daeed1f26e28bfcc367ed77247035c27a)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T07:20:53Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet): backward register budgets on SM100a, SM103a and SM107a (#9076)

`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet_train` is
the Cake kernel family for DeepSeek Sparse Attention training: top-k
sparse MLA with absorbed queries, 64 query heads, BF16, single rank. It
has two heads (RoPE: d_qk 576 / d_v 512; NoPE: d 512, K = V), and each
head has a forward and a backward. The backward comes in two layouts: a
default layout, and a natural layout that accumulates dK/dV directly
into a caller fp32 `dkv_acc` for packed trainer batches. There are also
key-pass builds for long key rows. In total that is 14 programs, each
built for sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a (42 builds). This PR regenerates
the package. The change that matters is the backward kernels' register
budgets on all three targets: the MMA-issue warps get more registers,
and on sm_107a the natural-layout reduce warps do too. The forward and
other kernels are regenerated from current sources with no intended
change. Compared with the previous Cake version (FlashInfer main at
fed9283), the backward is 1.021x-1.036x faster on the dense document
rows on all three GPUs, and 1.089x-1.144x faster on the packed, chunk
and tail rows on R200. Compared with cuDNN frontend 1.32.2, the new
package is faster on every row except the R200 dense-document backward
rows and most of the matching step rows. No deterministic Cake
implementation of this family exists yet, so there is no
deterministic-Cake comparison.

GPUs: B200 = NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, cc 10.0, 148 SMs, 1000 W); GB300 =
NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, cc 10.3, 152 SMs, 1400 W); R200 (sm_107a, cc
10.7, 212 SMs, 2300 W). CUDA driver API 13.4 on B200 and GB300, 13.5 on
R200. Kernels built with CUDA 13.4; torch 2.14.1+cu130. Each row runs in
its own process, with both sides on the same GPU and the same inputs.
Each latency is the CUPTI span from the first to the last GPU activity
of an iteration, with a cold L2, taken as the median over 10 rounds x 10
steps. Both sides are called through their public entry, including their
input/index glue: the Cake entry, and the cuDNN DSA sparse-attention
plans (trusted metadata, preallocated outputs) plus glue. `step` = fwd +
bwd. "vs previous Cake" = previous Cake ms / new Cake ms and "vs cuDNN"
= cuDNN ms / new Cake ms, so > 1 means the new package is faster. There
is no deterministic-Cake column because no deterministic Cake
implementation of this family exists. RoPE rows use top-k 2048, causal.
On R200, nope_glm53_a bwd (0.959x) is slower only in the full-step span,
because of host-side gaps; its kernel-only backward is unchanged (7.573
vs 7.574 ms), and so is its step (9.398 vs 9.401 ms).

### [91e76b2](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/91e76b20d38803ce95ebeb758a91ee7306571deb)

- **作者**: Brian K. Ryu
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T07:16:21Z
- **提交信息**: feat(batch_invariant): `softmax(batch_invariant=True)`, `sampling.log_softmax` and `sampling.log_probs`: the row log-sum-exp class `lse.row` (#8999)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Briefly describe the changes and why they’re
needed. -->

Brings batch invariance to select sampling kernels, similar to GEMMs. 
- `flashinfer.sampling.softmax(logits, temperature,
batch_invariant=True)` runs a specified, fingerprinted softmax in place
of the operator's kernels (in the input dtype, or in fp32 with
`out_dtype`)
- `flashinfer.sampling.log_softmax(logits, temperature)` returns the
fp32 log-softmax row
- `flashinfer.sampling.log_probs(logits, token_ids, temperature,
return_lse=)` returns the log-probability of one or `K` tokens per row
(and, with `return_lse`, the row's log-sum-exp).

Without the flag `softmax` is unchanged. 

**What is promised.** The chains above, stated in Lean and checked bit
for bit against their exact CPU model: run-to-run determinism
(CUDA-graph replay included), batch invariance (a row alone equals the
row inside any batch, at any position, in any sub-batch), configuration
and SM-count agreement (every member of the enumerated space gives the
same bits), and the shared dataflow of the three entries. Nothing is
promised relative to the operator's other softmax kernels or to torch.

**Contract.** bf16 / f16 / fp32 logits of shape `(..., N)`, any `N`;
temperature `None`, a positive scalar, or one per row (f16 / bf16 / f32
/ f64, the last rounded to f32); `token_ids` int32 / int64 of shape
`logits.shape[:-1]` or `logits.shape[:-1] + (K,)`; a row view whose
stride is a multiple of 16 bytes (the `[..., :vocab]` slice of a padded
lm_head) is read in place, other views are copied; `enable_pdl` (`None`
follows the device); M = 0 launches nothing. Anything else raises
`BatchInvariantUnsupportedError`; nothing falls back. `log_softmax` and
`log_probs` have no non-invariant implementation, and `out_dtype` needs
the flag. SM100 / SM103 / SM107.

### Where this fits the RL frameworks

Surveyed at the current heads of vLLM, SGLang, verl, Miles and NeMo RL,
on the paths their determinism / on-policy modes take
(`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`; SGLang `--enable-deterministic-inference`,
forced by `--rl-on-policy-target`; verl `full_determinism`; Miles
`--true-on-policy-mode`; NeMo RL `batch_invariant_mode` and its zero-KL
generation-parity preset):

* **All five compute the token log-probability on a full-vocabulary
row**: the engines gather the logits across tensor parallelism before
sampling, and the trainers' parity modes replace their
vocabulary-sharded normaliser by a gather of the full row (NeMo RL:
"per-rank partial normalizers round differently"; Miles all-gathers the
shards). The sharded default paths of the trainers are out of this PR's
scope.
* **The invariance mechanism is the same everywhere**: an
`aten::_log_softmax` override by a one-program-per-row Triton kernel in
vLLM, SGLang (installed by Miles's trainer too) and Megatron-Core (NeMo
RL); verl's rollout is vLLM's. The call shape is log-softmax then a
gather of one or several ids per row, the temperature applied by the
caller as a division of the logits beforehand (fp32 or bf16).
`log_softmax` is the entry those override points can take; `log_probs`
with `K` ids per row is the gather of the sampled token with its top-k
or requested alternatives.
* **Two callers agree bit for bit only when they call the same way**:
raw logits with the temperature (the class scales inside its chain) or
identically pre-scaled logits with `temperature=None`; vLLM's greedy
rows carry a temperature of 0, which maps to `None`. Left for later PRs:
autograd for the policy-loss sites (the parity modes keep the forward
and reuse the stock backward), tensor-parallel partials, the entropy the
trainers compute next to the log-prob.

Against the frameworks' own batch-invariant kernels:

| | this PR's entries | vLLM, SGLang, Megatron-Core batch-invariant
`log_softmax` |
|---|---|---|
| batch, position, SM-count invariance | by construction; stated in
Lean; fingerprinted | by construction (one program per row); no
statement beyond the docstring |
| run-to-run determinism | yes (graph replay included) | yes |
| temperature | in the kernel: a scalar or one per row | the caller
divides the logits first |
| outputs | the fp32 log-probs of one or `K` ids per row (+ `lse`), the
fp32 row, `softmax` in the input dtype or fp32 | the full row in the
input dtype, then torch gathers |
| arithmetic | fp32 `.rn` chains, `ex2.approx` / `lg2.approx` pinned per
architecture, an exact CPU model | fp32 Triton (bf16 end to end in
SGLang's RL mode); `tl.exp` is the same `ex2.approx` |
| vocabulary shards (TP) | no: a full row | no: a full row |
| autograd | no | the stock aten backward where the override is
installed |

### Performance against the frameworks' kernels

The frameworks' kernels are run from their own source as the frameworks
call them: vLLM's override (the fp32 cast of 16-bit logits, the kernel,
the gather), SGLang's deterministic mode (fp32 logits) and RL mode (bf16
end to end), Megatron-Core's kernel (NeMo RL); `torch` is
`log_softmax(dtype=float32)` + gather, or `torch.softmax`; `flashinfer`
is the operator's default route. Ratios are baseline time / ours (above
1: ours is faster), geometric mean and minimum over the regime's points.

### [911d6a9](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/911d6a9d62308b6c8a5249e8dc4aabc7518020f1)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T07:12:48Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda): preload the next task's entering state into tensor memory in the N16 work-bin build of BF16 KDA prefill (sm_103a) (#9075)

The Cake chunked KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) prefill behind
`flashinfer.recurrent_kda(..., backend="cake")` has modules with BF16
inputs and modules with TF32 inputs. Both come in fused and split forms.
The BF16-input fused module with FP32 state has work-binned builds,
which place several (sequence, head) tasks in each CTA's bin. These
builds come in an N32 variant and an N16 variant, with chunk sizes 32
and 16. In the bounded binned builds that prefetch the next task's
state, the compute warps load each task's FP32 entering state from
global memory. #9012 added a version of the N32 build that preloads this
state into tensor memory (TMEM). This PR adds the same preload to the
bounded N16 work-bin build with checkpoint TMA, on sm_103a (GB300) only.
In the new build, the prep stage that prepares a task's last chunk also
loads the next task's entering state into one of two TMEM slots. The
compute warps then copy the state from that slot and skip the global
load. A task skips the preload when it shares its state slot and head
with one of the six tasks before it in its bin. As a result, every task
reads the same FP32 state words that it reads without the preload. On
GB300, a launch uses the new build when the same four conditions hold as
for the N32 build: its work bins come from the strict bin test, it has
an initial state, every sequence has 64 to 256 tokens, and it has more
tasks than SMs. Every other launch keeps its build. On B200, every N16
work-bin launch keeps its build. Outputs, final states and checkpoints
are bitwise identical to FlashInfer main. The tables compare this PR
with FlashInfer main, which includes #9063, and report the latency per
call in microseconds. They have GB300 columns only, because sm_100a gets
no new program or route and every sm_100a program is SASS-identical to
FlashInfer main. Each table has 56 rows: 12 or 16 heads, no gate lower
bound or -5, and 14 sequence-length shapes. One table covers the
plan-cache fast path, and the other covers the serving pattern. TIE
means no difference beyond the measurement band. In each table, two rows
are faster. Both have 12 heads and gate lower bound -5. With shape BS16
x T64, the latency goes from 25.41 to 24.74 us (1.03x) on the fast path
and from 25.28 to 24.90 us (1.02x) in the serving pattern. With shape
BS64 x T64, it goes from 61.57 to 57.25 us (1.08x) on the fast path and
from 61.73 to 57.31 us (1.08x) in the serving pattern. Every other row
is TIE, and none is slower. On the fast path, the speedup is 1.00x to
1.08x over 56 rows. In the serving pattern, it is also 1.00x to 1.08x
over 56 rows. We also ran two sweeps of launch shapes on two GB300
nodes. In a 76-shape sweep, all 76 shapes are faster on both nodes. The
latency ratio (this PR / main) is 0.9241 to 0.9825 on one node and
0.9257 to 0.9854 on the other. In a fresh 58-shape sweep, the 38 shapes
that move to the new build are faster on both nodes, with median ratios
of 0.937 to 0.985. The 20 shapes that keep their build are TIE (0.999 to
1.0011), and none is slower. The other Cake variants are unchanged on
both sm_100a and sm_103a: the TF32-input modules, the split forms, the
N32 preload build and every other program.

GB300: NVIDIA GB300, sm_103a, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03. CUDA 13.4
(nvcc), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.

### [fdc2ee0](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/fdc2ee0964345c68b6a49909153865a7a7ddd8cd)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T07:07:02Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_kimi_k3_mla): add LSE, DCP and non-causal variants to the Cake Kimi-K3 MLA decode kernel (#9067)

`flashinfer.mla.cake_kimi_k3_mla`
(`trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla(..., backend="cake")`) is
Kimi-K3 MLA decode over an FP8 (E4M3) paged latent cache (latent 512 +
rope 64, page 64), with FP8 query and BF16 output. It ships 14 default
programs (row-tile main kernels, late-trigger tiles, two-CTA
`main_wide`, split-KV merge kernels), plus the B200-only persistent wide
route of #9066. This PR adds an extended variant of every default
program. The extended variant is selected only when the caller asks for
at least one of these:
- a caller-owned FP32 log-sum-exp output (`lse`, base e by default or
base 2)
- a decode-context-parallel interleaved KV-shard mask (`causal_seqs`,
`cp_world`, `cp_rank`)
- `causal=False` uniform multi-token speculative verify (#7809)

The baseline is TokenSpeed MLA 2.0.3
(`tokenspeed_mla.tokenspeed_mla_decode`), called exactly as vLLM's
TOKENSPEED_MLA backend calls it. At W=1 it is called with LSE output
requested so both sides produce LSE. Across 86 shapes, this PR's
extended variant has 57 WIN, 27 LOSS and 2 TIE against TokenSpeed.
TokenSpeed is faster mainly at the shortest global length (G 8195) and
at h96 DCP8 q1.

**NVIDIA GB300 (Blackwell, sm_103a, 152 SMs), CUDA 13.4, driver
580.159.03, torch 2.14.1.** Each latency is the median of 16 paired
interleaved slots per arm, on the same GPU with the same inputs. Speedup
= TokenSpeed / this PR (> 1 means this PR is faster), with an
order-statistic confidence interval. The verdict uses the cell's A/A
noise band. "Shipped default" is the existing Cake kernel without the
LSE / DCP / non-causal options.

Row names follow `<mode>_h<heads>_q<query tokens per request>_w<DCP
world>_<c=causal|n=non-causal>_G<global sequence length>_B<batch>_r<DCP
rank timed>`. Modes A-C are single-rank h12, D-F are h96 DCP8 and G-H
are h12 DCP8. With DCP8, each rank holds ceil((G - r)/8) keys per
request, and the timed kernel is one rank's. Rows r1..r7 are the rank
sweep and have no shipped-default measurement (shown as "-").

### [d227d0e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/d227d0eb86fbe4dc9f8ed66e711d138c37073561)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T06:58:17Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_mega_moe_v3): proxy fence in the carried programs, coherent loads of in-launch data (#9074)

This commit fixes two memory-ordering defects in mega_moe_v3. No defect was
seen to misbehave with CUDA 13.4.92, but the PTX memory model did not
guarantee the order the kernels rely on.

Proxy fence. Ten of the thirteen programs outside the TP / EP rank set read
data that other threads wrote in the same launch through the async proxy.
The nine pipeline programs (pipeline_fp4_t1, pipeline_fp4_t16_sm100a,
pipeline_fp4_t16_sm103a, pipeline_fp4_t128_sm100a, pipeline_fp4_t128_sm103a,
pipeline_fp4_t512, pipeline_fp4_t1024, pipeline_fp4_t4096 and
pipeline_fp8_t16) load the dispatch pool, PrivateSF1, PrivateSF2 and the FC1
output through TMA after an acquire, and their combine reads the expert
output rows that other CTAs stored with generic stores through bulk copies
after the l2_done acquire. grouped_fused loads its FC1 output through TMA
after the l1_arrival acquire. PTX orders a generic-proxy write before an
async-proxy read only behind a proxy fence, and these kernels had none. The
reading thread now issues fence.proxy.async.global after its acquire and
before the async-proxy read, as the TP / EP rank programs already do. Each
pipeline program gets two lines: the first statement of load_a's elected
block, and the statement right after the barrier that precedes the combine.
grouped_fused gets one line: the first statement of the elected block that
issues the A2 TMA load.

Coherent loads. Some kernels read a buffer that other CTAs write in the same
launch through a different __restrict__ pointer parameter. The compiler then
treats the buffer as read-only for the whole launch and emits
non-coherent loads (ld.global.nc). Such loads are defined only for data that
does not change during the kernel, and the compiler may move them across the
acquire that orders them after the writers.
- Ten TP / EP rank programs with the direct combine
  (pipeline_fp4_e384_i384_t1_sm103a, pipeline_fp4_e384_i384_t4_sm103a,
  pipeline_fp4_e384_i640_t1_sm103a, pipeline_fp4_e384_i640_t4_sm103a,
  pipeline_fp4_e48_i2304_t1_sm103a, pipeline_fp4_e48_i2304_t4_sm103a,
  pipeline_fp4_e48_i2304_t16_sm103a, pipeline_fp4_e96_i2304_t1_sm103a,
  pipeline_fp4_e96_i2304_t4_sm103a and pipeline_fp4_e96_i2304_t16_sm103a)
  read expert_output in the combine after the l2_done acquire, while the FC2
  epilogue of every CTA writes the same rows through PublicExpertOutput.
  expert_output and PublicExpertOutput are no longer __restrict__ in these
  kernels and in their binding declarations.
- grouped_fused reads the FC2 A scales through SFA2 after the l1_arrival
  acquire, while the FC1 epilogue of other CTAs writes them through SF_I_w
  (SFA2 is a uint32 view of SF_I_w). SF_I_w and SFA2 are no longer
  __restrict__ in the kernel and in the binding declaration, and the
  l1_arrival ld.acquire now has a "memory" clobber.
These loads are now ordinary global loads, which the existing release /
acquire chain orders after the writers.

The catalog changes only the closure_sha256 of these twenty programs. The
other twenty-five programs do not change.

### [9fe7f1a](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/9fe7f1aa7eb3a95f1b3ba62e05ef5879e5637c45)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T06:54:01Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det_train): sm_103a FP8 lets short calls take the wide unit from fewer tiles (#9065)

`flashinfer.cake_dsa_indexer_det_train.cake_dsa_indexer_det_train_topk`
is the deterministic DSA indexer top-k. It has two Cake variants: the
default BF16 form and the opt-in FP8 form (`float8_e4m3fn` q / k with a
per-key FP32 `k_scale`). This PR changes only the FP8 form, and only on
sm_103a. Earlier FP8 PRs:

- #8749 added the FP8 form and #8781 improved it.
- #8841 / #8895 / #8933 added an FP8 wide program on sm_103a / sm_100a /
sm_107a.
- #8954 picks the FP8 wide unit by wave count on sm_100a.
- #8976 made the sm_100a FP8 l6 programs load K_scale one tile ahead.
- #8986 added an FP8 l6 snake program on sm_107a for short
single-document calls.
- #9021 runs one-document sm_103a FP8 wide calls in the `:lsf` copy.
- #9047 picks the sm_103a FP8 wide unit by wave count.

The FP8 scan programs split queries into units. Narrow units hold 4
queries, l6 (three-warpgroup) units hold 6 and wide units hold 8. A
unit's waves on the persistent grid are ceil(ceil(T / queries per unit)
/ CTAs), and W = l6 waves / wide waves. For causal documents (key ratio
1), mean unit tiles = (Tkv - T / 2) / segments / 128.

Before this PR, the sm_103a FP8 record had `wide_wave_rule` = [1.7,
1.15, 64.0, 2048, 1.1, 112.0, 3.5, 14, 1.26, 40.0, 9.0] (#9047). In the
l6 range, the wide unit took a call when W >= 1.15 and the mean unit
tiles reached a floor:

- The floor is 64 for one document of at least 14 wide waves, plus 3.5
for each wide wave below 14. A short one-document call therefore needed
up to 64 + 13 * 3.5 = 109.5 mean unit tiles.
- On a packed call, the floor is at least 112.
- Below W = 1.26, the floor is at least 40 / (W - 1). On a packed call
it is then also at least 9 / (W - 1) ** 2.
- Above top-k 2048, the floor is multiplied by (top_k / 2048) ** 1.1.

This PR adds four elements to `wide_wave_rule` in the sm_103a FP8
record: 8.0, 55.0, 8 and 60.0. The rule is now [1.7, 1.15, 64.0, 2048,
1.1, 112.0, 3.5, 14, 1.26, 40.0, 9.0, 8.0, 55.0, 8, 60.0]. On one
document with fewer than 14 wide waves and W >= 1.26, the floor before
the top-k factor is now at most:

- 8 / (W - 1) ** 2;
- from two wide waves on, the larger of that and 55;
- from 8 wide waves on, the larger of that and 60.

Examples: 8 on one wide wave (W = 2), 55 at W = 1.5, 60 at 10 wide waves
and W = 1.4, and 72 at W = 4 / 3. The top-k factor (top_k / 2048) ** 1.1
still applies on top. Packed calls, calls of at least 14 wide waves and
calls below W = 1.26 keep their floor.

Below the new floor, boundary probes measured the l6 unit as fast as or
faster than the wide unit, so those calls stay on l6 (third table).
One-document wide calls from 64 mean unit tiles still use the `:lsf`
copy (#9021). The sm_100a FP8 rule (three elements) and all BF16 records
are unchanged, so their plans do not change.

The baseline is the previous Cake version: the FP8 dispatch on
FlashInfer main before this PR, which includes #9047. Ids and scores are
bit-identical between the two sides on all 65 measured rows.

**NVIDIA GB300, sm_103a (152 SMs), CUDA 13.4 (13.4.92), PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130.**

Each time is the CUPTI-measured GPU interval covering every kernel of
one call: scan, merge and finalize of a prepared runner into
caller-owned outputs and workspace. Settings are cold L2, eager launch,
3 warm-up iterations and 20 repetitions. The previous and this-PR arms
run in the same process. Each run's value is the median over three arm
orders (A then B, B then A, interleaved). The tables give the median
over 2 runs, which are separate processes on separate GPUs of one node.
"vs previous" = previous time / this PR time (above 1 = faster). An A/A
twin of each arm bounds the noise: a row counts as a speedup only when
every run and order exceeds 1 + the row's A/A band. "(parity)" marks a
row whose program changes but which did not pass that test. "(same
program)" marks a row where both sides run the same program, so it shows
parity by construction. Every row without either mark passed the test.

Of the 65 measured rows, the program changes on 39 (second table). Of
those 39, 33 are faster beyond the noise test (1.004x to 1.233x), 6 show
parity (SC7 1.011x, WB3 1.000x, WD12 1.000x, WD15 1.002x, WD16 1.002x,
WD25 1.000x) and none is slower. The geometric mean over the 39 changed
rows is 1.043x.

Owner shapes, all top-k 2048 and causal. P1 is a recorded packed
training call with 8 segments, and s2_4x2k_packed is 4 x 2048 queries
over 18432 / 43008 / 67584 / 100352 keys. All five already ran the wide
`:lsf` program after #9047, and this PR does not change them.
s2_4x2k_packed shows 1.015x even though both sides run the same program.
This is arm-position noise: the four arms of that row (this PR, its A/A
twin, previous, its A/A twin) all run the same program and measured
2.4424, 2.4591, 2.4635 and 2.4797 ms.

* **Improvements**
* Updated execution-policy thresholds for `sm_103a` FP8 wide scans.
Selection now considers wave count, document packing, `top_k`, and tile
characteristics, applying capped tile thresholds across different wave
configurations.

and caps. Existing packed-call floors and other wave-selection behavior
remain unchanged. These updates refine wide-unit selection for
qualifying inputs while preserving the existing rules outside the new
threshold conditions.

### [33d3f33](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/33d3f339adad5ed2504ad41edce7154fef03ec98)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T06:27:37Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_gemm_det_train): swap single-head weight gradients with a narrow side in the generic entry (#9070)

The Cake deterministic dense GEMM for training
(`flashinfer.cake_dense_gemm_det_train`) has two kernels. K1 is the
dense projection GEMM. K2 is the router GEMM. This PR changes only the
K1 planner. K2 is unchanged. The PR adds no kernel source and no new
compiled program, and it plans only registered programs. An unbatched (L
== 1) call of the generic entry `cake_dense_gemm_det_train_projection`
is a weight gradient when both operands are MN-major and there is no
transposed store. Before this PR, such a call kept the caller's
orientation, and a narrow side was padded into a 224- or 256-wide tile.
The planner now swaps two classes of these calls. The first class is
out_in (A = G.t(), B = X, output [d_out, d_in]) with 32 to 128 output
rows, plus 512 and 576. The rule table keys these rows only in the
swapped orientation. The call now gets the same plan as
`cake_dense_gemm_det_train_projection_wgrad` for the same math, so the
plan, the program and the bits are the same. On `sm_107a`, the bf16
6144->576 row swaps only from 6144 tokens. Below that, it keeps the
previous plan. The second class is in_out (A = X.t(), B = G, output
[d_in, d_out]) on `sm_100a` and `sm_103a` only. It applies when the
output has at most 64 columns and 4096 to 8192 rows, and K is at least
256 tokens. The swapped plan puts the narrow columns in the 64-row tile
of the transposed store. Every other call keeps its plan. The baseline
is the previous Cake version on main. Speedup = previous / this PR, so a
value above 1 means faster. Across 112 re-planned shapes, the speedup is
1.07x to 3.44x on GB300, 1.08x to 3.38x on GB200 and 1.09x to 3.68x on
B200. Across 57 re-planned rows, it is 1.19x to 3.62x on VR200. No
re-planned row is slower on any GPU. The 82 shapes whose plan is
unchanged measure 0.989x to 1.011x on the three `sm_100a` and `sm_103a`
GPUs. The 17 unchanged rows on VR200 measure 0.995x to 1.017x. Both
ranges are within noise.

*Table 1: re-planned shapes on GB300 (`sm_103a`, 152 SMs), GB200
(`sm_100a`, 152 SMs) and B200 (`sm_100a`, 148 SMs), CUDA 13.4. Times are
the CUPTI median span per call with a cold L2. Each value is the

## Summary by CodeRabbit

Co-authored-by: Avery Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [0b345ae](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/0b345aeca6cf630171ef2e1fc2643e6fe887984b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T06:26:19Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_lm_head_det_train): skip zero-weight policy rows and zero-dlogp log-probability rows (#9071)

`flashinfer.cake_lm_head_det_train` (deterministic LM-head projection +
fused loss) has five training variants: loss with `ce` or `policy`
objective, and log-probability with no, scalar or per-token temperature.
This PR skips zero-dlogp rows in the log-probability backward (dz
recompute and dW GEMMs stop at the live row count) and runs no gradient
work for zero-weight rows in the `policy` loss. Against the previous
Cake version of this kernel on main (cooled fwd+bwd), zero-dlogp shapes
are faster on 45/45 B200 shapes (1.040x to 1.301x) and 36/45 GB300
shapes (up to 1.281x; the other 9 parity or inconclusive, lowest 0.989),
and zero-weight policy shapes on 10/12 per GPU (up to 1.125x B200,
1.124x GB300). Shapes without zero rows show no change outside the noise
band (0.958 to 1.011); dX/dW bits may differ from the previous release
(within the existing accuracy bounds), but every run stays bitwise
repeatable.

**Legend:** `t<N>` N tokens; `ce`/`policy` loss objective;
`logprob`/`zd_*`/`fld_*` log-probability, temperature `p` none, `h`
per-token FP32, `s` scalar 0.7; `z166`/`z500` 16.6 %/50 % rows with zero
weight or zero dlogp, `random` or in groups of 512 (`group512`), `z0`
none; defaults chunk 4096, H 6144, V 154880, 5 % ignored rows (`c<N>`,
`h<H>v<V>`, `ign<pct>` override). A = previous Cake version on main, B =
this PR, A/B > 1 = B faster.

**B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs)**, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130: CUPTI GPU
ms per call, L2 flushed, median of 3 runs (3 nodes) x 4 rounds,
bootstrap CI95 of A/B.

1.4335] |

On this shape the gradient work of the live rows runs in the backward
instead of the forward, so that stage slows while the forward (1.42x)
and the whole step (1.109x, ckpt 1.060x) speed up.

### [e7c767d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e7c767d3bd3246e7880bcd9310643ba78fe8fc2f)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T06:10:14Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_gemm_nondet_train): router weight-gradient head/tail windows for 152-SM GB200 and GB300 (#9069)

The Cake dense GEMM ships as two packages: a deterministic one,
`flashinfer.cake_dense_gemm_det_train`, and a non-deterministic one,
`flashinfer.cake_dense_gemm_nondet_train`. This PR changes how the
non-deterministic package routes the FP32 router weight gradient (`dW =
G^T X`; 256 experts, hidden H, T tokens as the reduction dimension) on
152-SM GB200 and GB300. All other rows (GB300 H 5120, 148-SM B200/B300,
R200) route exactly as on current main.

- GB200 (sm_100a), H 5120: the head/tail atomic program `H0.5x3` now
also runs at T 16400-28672. It runs one head unit per CTA pair over half
of the steps and three tail units per pair, for 76 head and 228 tail
units on 152 SMs. Current main runs the deterministic plan through the
non-deterministic entry at these rows. The existing window, T
10240-16384, is unchanged, and T 16385-16399 keep the deterministic
plan.
- GB300 (sm_103a), H 6144: the `H1x5p44` head/tail window (44 head
units, then five tail units per CTA pair) now begins at T 16385 instead
of 16172 and still ends at 20480. T 16172-16384 therefore run the
deterministic 3-split plan.
- Router split counts: the non-deterministic package now takes them from
the deterministic package. This changes no route.

On GB200 the new route is faster than deterministic Cake, SOTA and
current main in every row. Speedups over the five shapes (T
16400-28672), shown as CUDA graph replay / eager with the geomean in
parentheses:

- Op: deterministic Cake 1.155-1.173x (1.166x) / 1.125-1.159x (1.140x);
SOTA 1.586-1.630x (1.616x) / 1.533-1.567x (1.551x); current main
1.153-1.165x (1.157x) / 1.074-1.135x (1.100x)
- Step: deterministic Cake 1.034-1.077x (1.061x) / 1.020-1.084x
(1.063x); SOTA 1.447-1.475x (1.462x) / 1.431-1.461x (1.444x); current
main 1.036-1.082x (1.055x) / 1.035-1.073x (1.055x)
- Checkpointed step: deterministic Cake 1.020-1.064x (1.042x) /
1.021-1.061x (1.041x); SOTA 1.480-1.541x (1.511x) / 1.461-1.501x
(1.487x); current main 1.020-1.050x (1.033x) / 1.025-1.033x (1.030x)

On GB300 the three changed shapes (T 16172, 16231, 16384) now run the
deterministic 3-split plan through the non-deterministic entry.
Speedups, shown as CUDA graph replay / eager with the geomean in
parentheses:

- Op: deterministic Cake 1.013-1.016x (1.015x) / 1.033-1.038x (1.036x);
SOTA 1.580-1.593x (1.588x) / 1.577-1.588x (1.583x)
- Step: deterministic Cake 1.016-1.022x (1.019x) / 1.024-1.031x
(1.028x); SOTA 1.472-1.497x (1.486x) / 1.470-1.480x (1.476x)
- Checkpointed step: deterministic Cake 0.995-0.999x (0.996x) /
1.002-1.011x (1.007x); SOTA 1.536-1.557x (1.548x) / 1.533-1.547x
(1.538x)

Under CUDA graph replay, the checkpointed step is slightly slower than
deterministic Cake at all three shapes. SOTA is not faster than the new
route in any row on either GPU.

Against the current main window (`H1x5p44`), measured entry vs entry on
one GB300 node, the result is mixed. In eager launches the op alone is
1.029-1.037x faster with the new route (geomean 1.033x). The step
(0.991-1.005x, geomean 0.996x) and checkpointed step (0.996-1.002x,
geomean 0.998x) stay within 1% either way. Under CUDA graph replay the
new route is slower at all three shapes. main/new is 0.980-0.986 for the
op (geomean 0.983), 0.982-0.998 for the step (0.988) and 0.985-0.996 for
the checkpointed step (0.989). So this PR adds a small CUDA graph
regression at GB300 H 6144, T 16172, 16231 and 16384.

## Router weight-gradient speedup tables

FP32 router weight gradient, 256 experts, hidden H, T tokens. PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130, cuBLAS 13.8.0.4. Times in µs: CUPTI span of the timed
kernels, cold L2. Except in the last table, each time is the median over
both nodes of per-run medians (2 nodes per GPU). Ratios > 1 mean the new
route is faster. op = router weight gradient alone; step = router
forward + input gradient + weight gradient; ckpt = checkpointed step, 2
x forward + input gradient + weight gradient. Deterministic Cake = the
router weight-gradient entry of `flashinfer.cake_dense_gemm_det_train`.
SOTA = the fastest correct (within the router FP32 accuracy budget)
non-Cake library call per row. That call is BF16x9-emulated FP32 cuBLAS:
`cublasSgemm` with `CUBLAS_FP32_EMULATED_BF16X9_MATH`, or, where marked

correct of the heuristic top 8). For step and ckpt, SOTA is the fastest
correct library launch per operation. Current main = the routing of the
row on FlashInfer main.

### [2095d60](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2095d60c93fc48f45685ed5ef93237fe9a53eeba)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T05:58:09Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_alpha_moe): NVFP4 fused batch kernel reduces two output blocks per bulk add on sm_103a (#9064)

The AlphaMoE Cake kernels in FlashInfer come in three sets: NVFP4 MoE,
W8A8 MoE and the fused router. This PR brings the pair-reduce change
from FlashInfer #8903, which shipped on sm_100a, to sm_103a (GB300). It
changes one NVFP4 kernel on sm_103a: the fused batch kernel of the
word-scale path. That kernel now places two adjacent 128-column
down-projection output blocks side by side, using one 1024-byte row per
routed token and a ring of two pair buffers. After the second block it
issues one FP32 bulk reduce per row, so it issues half as many reduces
and each one is twice as long. Every output element gets the same FP32
adds at the same addresses. Only the arrival order of the top_k adds can
change, which can already happen with the existing unordered bulk
reduces. Of the NVFP4 shapes below, only M=128, N=256, K=7168,
block_m=16 runs this kernel. On that shape, this PR is faster on GB300
than the previous version (the Cake AlphaMoE NVFP4 kernel from
FlashInfer #8903, now on main): 1.014x with memset and 1.015x with read.
The other shapes run the same machine code on both sides, with ratios of
0.999x to 1.000x. Speedup = previous / this PR, so a value above 1 means
this PR is faster.

#### GB300 (sm_103a)

NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a), driver 580.159.03, CUDA 13.3 (PyTorch 2.13, nvcc
13.3). Kernel time per MoE call in us: the per-call sum of the MoE
kernels' CUPTI durations, taking the median over iterations and over 6
interleaved rounds, then the median over 2 repetitions per GPU, then the
median over 4 GPUs per node, then the mean of 2 nodes. "memset" clears
L2 with a memset of a large buffer and "read" flushes L2 by reading a
large buffer. previous = the Cake NVFP4 kernel from FlashInfer #8903 on
main.

**memset**

| MoE | Shape | previous (us) | this PR (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| NVFP4 | M=8, N=256, K=7168, E=256, top_k=8, block_m=8 | 29.86 | 29.86
| 1.000x |
| NVFP4 | M=128, N=256, K=7168, E=256, top_k=8, block_m=16 | 91.22 |
89.98 | 1.014x |
| NVFP4 | M=8, N=1024, K=6144, E=256, top_k=8, block_m=8 | 68.48 | 68.48
| 1.000x |
| NVFP4 | M=128, N=1024, K=6144, E=256, top_k=8, block_m=8 | 210.53 |
210.59 | 1.000x |

**read**

| MoE | Shape | previous (us) | this PR (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| NVFP4 | M=8, N=256, K=7168, E=256, top_k=8, block_m=8 | 25.26 | 25.27
| 1.000x |
| NVFP4 | M=128, N=256, K=7168, E=256, top_k=8, block_m=16 | 79.94 |
78.73 | 1.015x |
| NVFP4 | M=8, N=1024, K=6144, E=256, top_k=8, block_m=8 | 55.05 | 55.11
| 0.999x |
| NVFP4 | M=128, N=1024, K=6144, E=256, top_k=8, block_m=8 | 195.61 |
195.58 | 1.000x |

The family's other Cake variants (the other NVFP4 routes, the W8A8 MoE
routes and the fused router) keep the same machine code, and the family
ships for sm_100a (B200) and sm_103a (GB300), with sm_100a (B200)
running the same machine code as before in this PR.

The Kimi-K3 MLA kernel `flashinfer.mla.cake_kimi_k3_mla`
(`trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla(..., backend="cake")`, FP8 E4M3
paged latent cache, FP8 query, BF16 output) ships 14 programs today.

kernel, paired with a tile-flag version of the 2-warp-per-row split-KV

### [8480055](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8480055a1737e353518be1b38eb06728ad5ab9da)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T05:23:35Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_kda_kcp): workspace bytes use the context device's architecture; strict #8928 names in the KCP parity test (#9058)

Follow-up to #9017 (KDA training packages named by mode, #8928) and
#9011 (CPU KCP partition parity test). The KDA KCP workspace-byte
queries now use the architecture of the context's device, not the
current CUDA device. The forward also plans with the context device's
architecture, so the byte query now matches the launch when the two
devices are different GPU models. This was raised in review of #8801.
The PR also fixes a stale registry key in the GDN nondet KCP test, and
the parity test now requires the final #8928 names. There are no kernel
or numerical behavior changes. The fix changes behavior only when the
current CUDA device differs from the context's device. The PR is based
on main at fed9283 (the #9017 merge) and has 4 commits across 6 files
(+322/-59).

### Changes

- **fix(cake_kda_det_kcp)** (6e2910c0)
- **Problem:** `cake_kda_det_train_kcp_workspace_bytes` in
`flashinfer/experimental/cake/cake_kda_det_train_kcp/cake_kcp_plan.py`
called the single-rank backend's `plan`, `workspace_bytes` and
`tables_bytes` without `arch`. Each call fell back to the current CUDA
device's architecture. The forward plans its local stages with the
architecture of its operands' device (`cake_jit.device_arch`). If the
current device was a different GPU model, the byte query could pick
other records and a different segment count than the launch.
- **Fix:** a private helper, `_device_arch(ctx.device)`, now passes each
context's own architecture to all three calls. It returns `None` for a
CPU device, a host without CUDA, or a device that no record targets. In
those cases the backend default applies, as before. When
`torch.cuda.is_available()` is False, the helper makes no CUDA call.
- **Tests:** 3 new CPU tests in
`tests/experimental/test_cake_kda_det_train_kcp_build.py` spy on the
three calls. They check two cases:
- A context on `cuda:1`, with current device `cuda:0` of a different
architecture, passes the context's architecture.
- Without CUDA, all three calls get `arch=None` and no CUDA call is
made.
- **fix(cake_kda_nondet_kcp)** (c9c03aa4): the same fix and tests for
`cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp_workspace_bytes` in
`flashinfer/experimental/cake/cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp/cake_kcp_plan.py`.
The tests are in
`tests/experimental/test_cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp_build.py`.
- **test(cake_gdn_nondet_kcp)** (3449ac67): a one-line change in
`tests/experimental/test_cake_gdn_nondet_train_kcp.py`. The call
`cake_package("cake_kda_det_train_kcp", ...)` becomes
`cake_package("cake.cake_kda_det_train_kcp", ...)`, which is the
deterministic KDA KCP registry key after #9017. With the old key, the
opt-in `test_plan_parity_with_kda_on_rows` cases raised `KeyError`.
These cases run only when `GDN_ROWS_DIR` is set, and default runs skip
them.
- **test(cake_kcp)** (b1db93bd):
`tests/cpu/test_cake_kcp_partition_parity.py` now requires the final
#8928 names, since every renamed package is on main:
- A package row's import path must end in `cake_<op>_<mode>_train_kcp`,
with op in {kda, gdn} and mode in {det, nondet}.
- The entries must be exactly `cake_<op>_<mode>_train_kcp_partition` and
`cake_<op>_<mode>_train_kcp_build_context`.
- A KDA or GDN KCP row or entry under any other name fails the test.
Examples are the pre-#8928 `cake_<op>_train_kcp` and
`partition_det_kcp`.

The error-message mask used to hide any word containing "kcp". It now
hides only each package's own names: its `cake_<op>_<mode>_train_kcp`
prefix and its `Cake<OP><Mode>Kcp` class prefix. This addresses the
review note on #9011.

### Tests

All at head b1db93b.

- **CPU:**
- The KDA det/nondet KCP build, api and names tests, the KCP partition
parity test (129 passed), the standalone package test (60 passed, 1
xfailed) and the manifest checker all pass.
- The negative control for the strict parity rule passes 8 of 8: the
test rejects old-style rows and entries.
- The 3 new tests in each build file fail against the unfixed modules,
as a negative control.
- **GDN rows** (`GDN_ROWS_DIR` set, 107 rows):
`test_plan_parity_with_kda_on_rows` passes 107 of 107 in
`test_cake_gdn_nondet_train_kcp.py` and 107 of 107 in
`test_cake_gdn_det_train_kcp.py`. The same 107 nondet cases fail with
`KeyError` on main.
- **GPU, GB300 with 4 GPUs:**
- `test_cake_kda_det_train_kcp_dist.py`: 23 passed, 3 skipped (8-GPU
cases).
- `test_cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp_dist.py`: 25 passed, 3 skipped (8-GPU
cases).
- The det and nondet build files: 39 and 40 passed, with the 6 new tests
running with CUDA visible.
- **Targeted CI:** all jobs pass, covering the 4 changed test files, the
AOT builds and pre-commit.

With `GDN_ROWS_DIR` set, 36 `test_row_cost_rule_on_rows_of_record` /
`test_row_cost_lpt_rule_on_rows_of_record` cases fail identically on
main and on this branch. They are pre-existing, unrelated to this PR,
and skipped in default runs.

### [3488421](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3488421f205be9691883eec9be94d7adec96fecf)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T05:14:59Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda): enable the tensor-memory next-state preload work-bin build of BF16 KDA prefill on B200 (sm_100a) (#9063)

The Cake chunked KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) prefill behind
`flashinfer.recurrent_kda(..., backend="cake")` has modules with BF16
inputs and modules with TF32 inputs. Both come in fused and split forms.
The BF16-input fused module with FP32 state has work-binned builds,
which place several (sequence, head) tasks in each CTA's bin. One of
them is the bounded binned build that prefetches the next task's state.
In that build, the compute warps load each task's 64 KiB FP32 entering
state from global memory. #9012 added a new version of that build for
sm_103a (GB300) that preloads this state into tensor memory (TMEM). In
the new build, the prep stage that prepares a task's last chunk also
loads the next task's entering state into one of two TMEM slots. The
compute warps then copy the state from that slot and skip the global
load. A task skips the preload when it shares its state slot and head
with one of the six tasks before it in its bin. As a result, every task
reads the same FP32 state words that it reads without the preload. Until
now, this build ran only on GB300. This PR enables the same build, with
the same kernel code, on sm_100a (B200). On B200, a launch now uses this
build when the same four conditions hold as on GB300: its work bins come
from the strict bin test, it has an initial state, every sequence has 64
to 256 tokens, and it has more tasks than SMs. Every other launch keeps
its build, including launches whose bins come from the bounded rule.
Outputs are bitwise identical to FlashInfer main. The tables compare
this PR with FlashInfer main on B200 and report the latency per call in
microseconds. We measured against FlashInfer main before #9040 merged.
#9040 changed only sm_103a, and every sm_100a program on current main is
SASS-identical to the measured baseline, so the baseline still holds.
Each table has 56 rows: 12 or 16 heads, no gate lower bound or -5, and
14 sequence-length shapes. One table covers the plan-cache fast path,
and the other covers the serving pattern. TIE means no difference beyond
the measurement band. In each table, two rows are faster. Both have 16
heads and gate lower bound -5. With shape BS16 x T64, the latency goes
from 24.99 to 23.74 us (1.05x) on the fast path and from 24.99 to 23.62
us (1.06x) in the serving pattern. With shape BS64 x T64, it goes from
67.23 to 65.22 us (1.03x) on the fast path and from 67.68 to 65.22 us
(1.04x) in the serving pattern. Every other row is TIE, and none is
slower. On the fast path, the speedup is 1.00x to 1.05x over 56 rows. In
the serving pattern, it is 0.99x to 1.06x over 56 rows, and two TIE rows
read 0.99x. We also ran two sweeps of held-out launch shapes on two B200
nodes. In a 64-shape sweep, 62 shapes are faster on one node and 59 on
the other, the rest are TIE, and none is slower. The latency ratio (this
PR / main) is 0.9471 to 0.9990 on the first node and 0.9467 to 0.9995 on
the second. In a fresh sweep with 108 timed shapes, 50 shapes are faster
on one node and 48 on the other, the rest (58 and 60) are TIE, and none
is slower. GB300 is unchanged because no sm_103a build or route changes,
so the tables have B200 columns only. The other Cake variants (the
TF32-input modules, the split forms and every other program) are
unchanged on both sm_100a and sm_103a.

B200: NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, 148 SMs, driver 580.82.07. CUDA 13.4 (nvcc),
PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.

### [7828a1d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7828a1d860c749c0a4eda4346da7f2dd02419319)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T05:07:33Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): sm_103a FP8 paged-context form programs with the 4-stage K/V ring (#9062)

Cake's FP8 paged-context attention kernel (FP8 Q/K/V, head dim 128)
ships AOT runtime-size programs at GQA packs 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12 and
16. Each pack comes in six forms. One is plain causal. The other five
are flag forms: NC (non-causal), LSE (causal with LSE output), SINK
(causal with sinks), NC_LSE and NC_SINK.

On sm_103a (GB300), the plain causal programs already use a 4-stage K/V
ring with the swapped P tile (the `_PX` builds). Until now, the five
flag forms used a 3-stage K/V ring program (`RUNTIME_PACK<p>_<FORM>`).

This PR adds 45 sm_103a programs, `RUNTIME_PACK<p>_<FORM>_PX` (5 forms x
9 packs). They use the 4-stage ring and the swapped P tile. On sm_103a,
flag-form calls with more than 128 keys now take the `_PX` program of
the same pack. Calls with 128 keys or fewer keep the 3-stage program.
sm_100a (B200) routing is unchanged.

The 80 routed rows run 1.053x-1.171x faster than the previous program.
They are also faster in each of the 10 memory layouts. No row is slower.

- **form**: NC is non-causal. LSE is causal with LSE output. SINK is
causal with sinks. NC_LSE and NC_SINK are their non-causal versions.
- **batch x q x kv**: batch x query tokens x key/value tokens per
request.
- **q/kv heads**: query heads / KV heads.
- **page**: KV page size in tokens.
- **program**: the program this PR routes the row to on sm_103a. "JIT
(unchanged)" marks the 5 rows at 128 x 1 x 16384. These rows keep the
JIT module.
- **previous Cake µs**: the 3-stage form program on FlashInfer main
before this PR. For the "JIT (unchanged)" rows it is the JIT module.
- **this PR µs**: the program in the **program** column.
- **trtllm-gen µs**: trtllm-gen on the same shape, shown for comparison.
- **previous/PR** and **trtllm-gen/PR**: ratios of the shown medians. A
ratio above 1 means this PR is faster.

The family also ships BF16 paged-context programs on sm_100a and
sm_103a, and these FP8 paged-context programs also ship on sm_100a.

### [50d7194](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/50d71949c9b79000d619bc6751e1246a148b4648)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T05:01:57Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_gemm_nondet_train): exact-FP32 cluster SIMT router forward at 1 to 192 tokens on 212-SM sm_107a (#9060)

The Cake dense GEMM ships as two packages: a deterministic one,
`flashinfer.cake_dense_gemm_det_train`, and a non-deterministic one,
`flashinfer.cake_dense_gemm_nondet_train`. This PR speeds up the FP32
router forward (`out = X @ W.T`) in the non-deterministic package on
212-SM R200 (sm_107a), with 256 experts and hidden H 4096/5120/6144. It
builds the two exact-FP32 cluster SIMT router forward programs for
sm_107a. For every H, it routes T 1-8 to `simt_c8_kg4_l32_e8t4` and T
9-192 to `simt_c8_ffma_l16_e16t32`. Other sm_107a SM counts (208, 216)
keep the current route.

Under CUDA graph replay, the forward op is 1.330-4.604x faster than the
deterministic Cake package (geomean 2.445x). It is 1.264-4.415x faster
than the current main route (H4096 1.264-3.859x, H5120 1.284-4.090x,
H6144 1.312-4.415x). Over deterministic Cake, the whole training step is
1.290-3.899x faster (geomean 2.348x) and the checkpointed step is
1.329-4.535x faster (geomean 2.447x). Compared with the current route,
the new route needs 0.410-0.895x the time for the step and 0.299-0.852x
for the checkpointed step, so it is faster in every row. In eager mode,
the op is 1.365-4.416x faster than deterministic Cake (geomean 2.438x)
and 1.309-4.281x faster than the current route. In the same mode, the
step is 1.340-3.750x faster than deterministic Cake (geomean 2.325x) and
the checkpointed step is 1.362-4.350x faster (geomean 2.414x).

The cuBLAS baseline is `torch.mm` in FP32 with TF32 off
(`fp32_precision='ieee'`). In every row it was the fastest library arm
within the router accuracy budget, ahead of BF16x9-emulated
`cublasSgemm`. Against it the ratios are as follows (CUDA graph / eager,
geomean in parentheses):

- Op: 0.790-2.746x (1.281x) / 0.832-2.677x (1.304x)
- Step: 0.807-2.034x (1.210x) / 0.805-1.943x (1.202x)
- Checkpointed step: 0.841-2.402x (1.248x) / 0.869-2.319x (1.261x)

Under CUDA graph replay, cuBLAS is faster in 9 op rows, 7 step rows and
9 checkpointed-step rows, out of 54 each. In all three it is faster at
H4096 T1/T160/T176/T192 and H6144 T1. It is also faster in the op at
H5120 T176/T192 and H6144 T176/T192. In the step it is also faster at
H5120 T1/T176. In the checkpointed step it is also faster at H5120
T1/T176/T192 and H6144 T176.

## Router forward speedup tables

NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs), driver 620.43, CUDA 13.4 (nvcc 13.4.92),
PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, cuBLAS 13.8.0.4; CUPTI span of the operation's
kernels, cold L2, CUDA graph replay; median of per-run medians over 2
nodes x 4 runs. FP32 router, 256 experts, hidden H, T tokens.
Deterministic Cake = `flashinfer.cake_dense_gemm_det_train`. cuBLAS
(SOTA) = `torch.mm` FP32 with TF32 off (`fp32_precision='ieee'`), the
fastest library arm within the router accuracy budget at every row
(other arm: BF16x9-emulated `cublasSgemm`). For the step and
checkpointed step, cuBLAS is the fastest correct library launch per
operation. Step = forward + input gradient + weight gradient;
checkpointed step = 2 x forward + input gradient + weight gradient. The
input and weight gradients use the respective package's programs. Times
in µs; ratios > 1 mean the new route is faster.

### [7cb00fd](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7cb00fde4a579dc41d4613ac56f28551eb373001)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T04:57:08Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mega_moe): sm_107a fence-free push combine for the BF16 rank-major EP8 layer (#9061)

This PR updates the Cake-generated BF16 rank-major expert-parallel EP8
layer of the `MoEEpLayer` mega backend (`cake_mega_moe`). The layer uses
BF16 activations, weights and output, hidden size 7168, intermediate
size 2048, 256 experts (32 per rank), top-8 routing over 8 ranks, and 1
to 128 tokens per rank. It has one variant (BF16, rank-major, EP8), and
this PR changes only its sm_107a build. The sm_100a build is
byte-identical. Above 32 tokens per rank, the unpermute kernel now
pushes each routed partial row to its source rank with plain stores, and
the combine sums the local rows instead of running the fenced pull
combine. Route codes are now built in the staging kernel, the
low-latency receive polls early, and the combine adds L2 prefetch hints.
Outputs are bitwise identical to the previous version. Against the
previous Cake version on FlashInfer main, speedups range from 1.000x to
1.040x. Against the strongest non-Cake baseline, NVLink one-sided
all-to-all (Lamport transport) + TensorRT-LLM BF16 MoE, they range from
1.011x to 1.244x. The other sm_107a baselines tested, NVLink two-sided +
TensorRT-LLM and CuTe-DSL MoE, are slower. The smallest gain over main
is random routing at 4 tokens per rank in graph mode, which is at parity
(183.67 us vs 183.62 us).

GPUs in one NVLink domain, CUDA 13.4 toolkit, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130,
driver 620.69. Each row times the full layer forward in eager or
CUDA-graph mode with cold L2. Each value is the median over 8 rounds of
the slowest rank's per-rank median of 20 iterations. All arms ran
interleaved in the same job, and the baseline value is the fastest of 3
autotuned replicas. `all_ranks` routing places each token's 8 experts on
8 different ranks; `random` takes the top 8 of 256 experts from random
scores.*

The other Cake MegaMoE variants in FlashInfer are SM90 BF16 (sm_90a),
MXFP8 EP16 (sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a), SM120 MXFP4 x MXFP8 (sm_120a)
and the top-k reduce (sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a), and the BF16
rank-major layer ships on sm_100a and sm_107a.

### [46ff3ec](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/46ff3eca2e2dd0e66eb8d8e231973062543497fe)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T04:47:40Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det_train): plain l6 order for packed and few-wave sampling-off calls on sm_107a (#9052)

Cake ships two variants of its deterministic DSA indexer top-k training
kernel (`cake_dsa_indexer_det_train_topk`) in FlashInfer: the default
BF16 form and the opt-in FP8 (e4m3) form. Each form has a
sampled-threshold mode and a sampling-off mode, and the family ships on
sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a. This PR changes only the BF16 plan policy
on sm_107a and adds no new programs. Packed (multi-document) calls now
use the plain l6 order instead of the snake order. The exceptions are
calls sampled with mean unit tiles >= 48 or within 7 l6-grid waves. Some
sampling-off calls have no registered snake l6 program. At <= 310
pair-wide waves, they now fall back to the plain l6 program instead of
staying on the paired wide snake program. Output ids and scores are
bit-identical.

The baseline is the previous Cake version, FlashInfer main `0ff7d4fb`.
Speedup is main time divided by this PR time, so values above 1 mean
faster. The largest gains are on sampling-off calls that leave the
pair_wide snake program. The one-segment 16384 x 32k grid goes from
2.4476 to 2.0110 ms (1.217x). Its 2-, 4- and 8-segment versions reach
1.208x, 1.189x and 1.181x. The single 262k causal document goes from
141.1868 to 137.8495 ms (S6, 1.024x). With sink statistics it goes from
124.4734 to 120.9001 ms (S6sink, 1.030x). The 47 packed row-modes that
leave the l6 snake order range from 1.001x to 1.039x. The top value is
E8x16k_k512 with sampling off, 6.1746 to 5.9453 ms. Rows whose program
does not change stay between 0.993x and 1.011x.

| sm_107a (212 SMs, CUDA 13.4) | min | max |
|---|---|---|
| sampling off, `pair_wide snake -> l6` (6 rows) | 1.024x (S6) | 1.217x
(G16384x32k_s1) |
| packed calls, sampling on, `l6 snake -> l6` (8 rows) | 1.001x
(E4x8k_k2048) | 1.022x (E8x8k_k2048) |
| packed calls, sampling off, `l6 snake -> l6` (39 rows) | 1.001x
(E8x32k_k512, E16x64k_k2048) | 1.039x (E8x16k_k512) |
| packed and segment-grid shapes, program unchanged (34 row-modes) |
0.993x (G4096x8k_s2) | 1.010x |
| prepared calls, sampling on, program unchanged (32 rows) | 0.996x (V1)
| 1.011x (Z1k4096) |
| prepared calls, sampling off, program changed (4 rows: S6, S6sink, Z2,
Z3; same measurements as above) | 1.006x (Z3) | 1.030x (S6sink) |
| prepared calls, sampling off, program unchanged (28 rows) | 0.993x
(S2) | 1.005x (Z1k4096, Z1k256, Z2cp) |
| eager entry, program unchanged (8 rows) | 0.999x (S1, S2, Z2cp) |
1.006x (A2) |

## Measured results

Only sm_107a is timed: this PR changes only BF16 sm_107a plans (checked
plan geometries that change: 630 of 17534 on 212 SMs, 606 of 17534 on
208 SMs); the sm_100a and sm_103a plans and every FP8 plan are
unchanged. "this PR" was timed on top of main 0ff7d4fb. Plan "unchanged"
means both sides launch the same program; "snake" is the snake key-tile
order, the other programs walk key tiles in plain order.

### [593b960](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/593b96051ea660d1cd44075d5b006cd8d3b65c13)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T04:29:51Z
- **提交信息**: refactor(cake_gqa_nondet_train): keep default_workspace internal to cake_backend (#8928) (#9054)

Part of #8928, following #8939 and #8962. Rule 7 of #8928 says every
public name except ALL_CAPS constants must carry the mode word.

`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_gqa_nondet_train` still imported
`default_workspace` from `cake_backend` and listed it in the package
`__all__`. The names test also allowed it by name.
`docs/training_backend_names.md` calls it an internal backend helper
that keeps its name. Because anything in the package `__all__` is
public, the export conflicted with rule 7 and with that doc.

- The package `__init__.py` no longer imports or exports
`default_workspace`. It stays in `cake_backend` and in
`cake_backend.__all__` with the other internal helpers. It is not
renamed or aliased.
- `tests/experimental/test_cake_gqa_nondet_train_names.py` drops the
by-name allowance. Every package `__all__` name must now be a forwarded
mode-word object or an ALL_CAPS constant. A new check confirms that the
backend's internal helpers are not package attributes. These are the
non-constant `cake_backend.__all__` names the facade does not forward,
including `default_workspace`.
- `docs/training_backend_migration.md` gets a row for the old name in
the GQA HD256 table.

Behavior doesn't change. When an entry point gets `workspace=None`, it
still calls `cake_backend.default_workspace(device_index)` internally.
Kernels, the build and the facade are unchanged. Nothing else in the
library, tests, scripts or docs uses the package-level name.

## Migration

| Old name | In | New location |
|---|---|---|
| `flashinfer.experimental.cake_gqa_train.default_workspace` | 0.7.3,
0.7.4rc1 |
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_gqa_nondet_train.cake_backend.default_workspace`
(internal; not exported by the package or the facade) |

Calls that pass `workspace=None` already use this per-stream default
workspace. To pass a workspace explicitly, create one with
`flashinfer.cake_gqa_nondet_train.cake_gqa_nondet_train_workspace`.

**Tests:** head 511c0e60, CPU x86_64:
`tests/experimental/test_cake_gqa_nondet_train_names.py`,
`tests/cpu/test_cake_mode_names.py`,
`tests/experimental/test_containment.py` and
`tests/cpu/test_cake_packages_standalone.py`: 122 passed, 3 xfailed,
same as main c7f959a4. pre-commit and `scripts/check_pr_document.py`
report nothing new.

### [6910fe4](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/6910fe4b686bf044ff7a23fed9c7574526eb8193)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T04:17:15Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kimi_k3_fp8_projection): SM100a grouped tile raster with two TMEM accumulators for TP8 q_proj M 4097..16384 (#9059)

`flashinfer.gemm.kimi_k3_fp8_projection` (experimental, backend
`"cake"`) computes the TP-local projection GEMMs of Kimi-K3. Cake ships
one data-type/layout variant of this kernel. It takes row-major BF16
activations quantized per token to E4M3 with 1x128 UE8M0 scales and E4M3
`[N, K]` weights with 128x128 UE8M0 block scales. It accumulates in FP32
and outputs BF16. This PR updates that variant. The baseline is the
previous Cake version, which is current FlashInfer main.

What changes:
- sm_100a (B200) only: the 192-wide, 128-K TMA-store GEMM program gets a
twin. The twin walks its output tiles in raster groups of 4 CTA row
tiles and gives each CTA pair two tensor-memory accumulators, so the MMA
warp starts the next tile while the epilogue drains the previous one.
Each tile's MMA sequence, K order and scales are unchanged. The twin is
used for M 4097 to 16384 of the TP8 q_proj projection (N 1536, K 7168).
In the table that is one shape, TP8 q_proj M = 16384.
- sm_103a (GB300): no change. Its programs and routes are identical to
main, so GB300 was not re-measured and the table covers B200 only.

On B200, TP8 q_proj M = 16384 goes from 172.192 us to 168.944 us, a
1.019x speedup. That is the median of 10 paired interleaved rounds, and
the per-round ratios span 1.0175-1.0216. The other 197 shapes run the
same programs as main. Their ratios are 0.996-1.005 (median 1.000), with
20 above and 28 below 1.000 at 3 decimals. The lowest is TP1 fused_qkvg
M = 4096 (0.996, per-round 0.9060-1.1110) and the highest is TP1 o_proj
M = 16384 (1.005). Across all 198 shapes, ratios are 0.996-1.019 (median
1.000), with 21 above and 28 below 1.000 at 3 decimals.

The shape list does not include the other TP8 q_proj M values in the new
twin's launch range. They were measured on B200 in a separate 10-round
interleaved pass:

| M | main (us) | PR (us) | speedup |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 4097 | 52.032 | 52.032 | 1.000 |
| 6144 | 73.344 | 73.184 | 1.002 |
| 8192 | 96.064 | 94.944 | 1.012 |
| 12288 | 140.368 | 137.288 | 1.022 |
| 16383 | 172.032 | 168.536 | 1.021 |

Output is bit-identical to FlashInfer main on B200 for all 198 shapes
and for the extra M values above. GB300 runs the same programs as main.

NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a), CUDA 13.4. `main (us)` and `PR (us)` are the
median per-call latency in microseconds for FlashInfer main and this PR.
`speedup` is the median of per-round paired ratios (FlashInfer main /
this PR) over 10 to 16 interleaved rounds on the same GPU, so it can
differ from the ratio of the two medians.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
* Added a Kimi K3 FP8 projection option for supported SM100 workloads,
with updated dispatch for a specific configuration.

* **Bug Fixes**
* Improved consistency of large offset calculations across projection
paths, reducing the risk of incorrect addressing in large workloads.

* **Tests**
  * Updated projection routing checks to cover the new option.

### [df6d845](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/df6d8455396805243fa60772c364c4c9bb5aa36c)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T04:06:44Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda_det): roll the sm_107a token-row drains of the det GLM intra kernels (follow-up to #7817) (#9048)

Follow-up to #7817.

In the deterministic single-rank KDA training backend on sm_107a, the
token-row GLM-intra kernels for the g:off form (FP32 gate) and the
raw:off form (BF16 raw gate activated in the kernel) now run all four
token-row drains as rolled loops; neither form uses in-kernel L2 norm.
The row operations run in the same order, so outputs are bitwise
identical, and the sm_100a/sm_103a SASS is unchanged. Each timing is the
median of 15 samples of 20 back-to-back backward-only or
forward+backward steps, measured with CUDA events (warm L2, eager, head
dim 128, BF16 q/k/v), with before and after alternated in ABBA order
twice on an otherwise idle GPU; speedup = before/after, where before is
the same kernels on main without this change.

toolkit, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.**

The deterministic KDA training family also has fused in-kernel L2 norm
forms, saved-set and recomputed (checkpoint) backward, and a
context-parallel (KCP) package, plus a non-deterministic package that
picks up the same two kernels, all built for sm_100a, sm_103a, and
sm_107a.

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [2e4114e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2e4114ec93754ec1413f39a60b98a7ebc0fc697a)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T04:05:17Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn_nondet_train): split the fused forward scan and output over the value halves on R200 (#9056)

FlashInfer ships four Cake GDN (gated delta net) training packages. They
come in deterministic and non-deterministic forms, and each form has a
single-rank package and a key-sharded context-parallel (KCP) package.
All four take BF16 q / k / v with head dim 128.

This PR changes only the non-deterministic single-rank package,
`flashinfer.cake_gdn_nondet_train`, and only on sm_107a (R200). Some
shapes leave the GPU under-filled when the fused forward scan-and-output
runs as one launch. On those shapes, each CTA now covers one half of the
128-wide value dimension, so the launch has twice the CTAs. The
deterministic package already uses this split, with the same selection
rule, on sm_107a. The backward is unchanged. In the benchmark set the
split engages on three shapes, which are starred in the tables. Every
other shape launches the same kernels as main.

Ratio = baseline ms / this PR ms (> 1 means this PR is faster). FP32
beta (the benchmark default) unless noted:

- **vs ND main** (this package at main `3053bd07`, the previous version
of this kernel)
- fwd on the starred shapes r07_1x16384_h8 / pair_h2_hv6 / pair_h1_hv3:
1.0277 / 1.0367 / 1.0858
  - fwd+bwd on the same shapes: 1.0131 / 1.0157 / 1.0285
  - ckpt on the same shapes is parity: 1.0062 / 0.9980 / 0.9961
- All 45 cells (15 shapes x 3 ops), after the re-measure: 2 WIN, 43
PARITY, 0 slower. BF16 beta: 4 WIN, 41 PARITY.
- **vs det** (`flashinfer.cake_gdn_det_train` at `3053bd07`)
  - r07_1x16384_h8: fwd+bwd 1.0401, ckpt 1.0259
  - pair_h1_hv3: fwd+bwd 1.0964
- All 45 cells in the first run: 8 WIN, 34 PARITY, 3 LOSS_ONE, 0
REGRESSION.
- BF16 beta: 7 WIN, 37 PARITY and one slower cell, r07_1x16384_h8
fwd+bwd at 0.9897. det is about 1 % faster there because it has a
BF16-beta-specific backward that the non-deterministic package does not
have yet.
- **vs non-Cake**: the fastest per cell of cuDNN frontend 1.32.1 FROST
(ck64 / ck0) and FLA 0.6.0 Triton. These are the strongest non-Cake GDN
implementations on sm_107a. FROST was fastest in every cell, and
FlashQLA has no sm_107a build.
- This PR is faster on fwd+bwd and ckpt for every shape (1.0886 to
2.6054).
- FROST ck0 is faster on the forward alone for most shapes (0.4591 to
0.9474 on those cells).

- **Setup:** one R200 GPU (VR200, sm_107a, 212 SMs), driver 620.43,
PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0 runtime), Cake kernels compiled with
nvcc 13.4. Eager execution (no CUDA graphs), warm JIT cache, 256 MiB L2
flush before every sample, CUDA events.
- **Timing:** 8 processes in A B B A A B B A arm order. Each process
times every shape and op in 6 groups, and each group interleaves this PR
and the baseline (3 warm-up + 16 samples per call). ms = median of the
per-process medians. Non-Cake arms ran in 2 of the 8 processes.
- **Rows:** shape = (H query/key heads, HV value heads, document
lengths) from the ROWS / PACKS / PAIRS tables in
`benchmarks/bench_cake_gdn_nondet_train.py`, head dim 128. Ops: fwd;
fwd+bwd; ckpt = 2 x forward + backward under torch checkpoint.
- **Columns:** shape, op, ND main ms, det ms, non-Cake ms (impl), this
PR ms, vs ND main, vs det, vs non-Cake.
- **Classes:**
- WIN / REGRESSION: faster / slower beyond the same-code A/A noise band
in both replicates (4 processes each)
  - PARITY: within the noise band
  - LOSS_ONE: slower in only one replicate
  - UNSTABLE: the two replicates disagree
- **Markers:**
- Star: the split engages (on 208-, 212- and 216-SM R200 parts).
Unstarred rows launch the same kernels as main, so their ratios against
ND main show noise only.
  - Dagger: re-measured in the last table.

#### Re-measure of the two dagger cells (FP32 beta)

In the first run, the FP32 fwd+bwd cells r01_4x4096_h8 and
r02_real3x4.25k_h8 were slower than ND main, even though their launches
are identical to main. A re-measure with 4 more processes classed both
as PARITY (0.9964 and 0.9988 vs ND main).

| shape | op | ND main ms | det ms | this PR ms | vs ND main | vs det |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| r01_4x4096_h8 | fwd+bwd | 0.3900 | 0.3911 | 0.3914 | 0.9964 PARITY |
0.9992 PARITY |
| r02_real3x4.25k_h8 | fwd+bwd | 0.3340 | 0.3342 | 0.3344 | 0.9988
PARITY | 0.9994 PARITY |

The other three packages (`flashinfer.cake_gdn_det_train`,
`flashinfer.cake_gdn_det_train_kcp`,
`flashinfer.cake_gdn_nondet_train_kcp`) are unchanged; all four ship on
sm_100a (B200), sm_103a (GB300) and sm_107a (R200), and on sm_100a and
sm_103a this package launches the same kernels as main for every shape,
so those architectures have no timing rows.
