Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [a0be64f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a0be64f36987d14a110797a517b4262c480dab8a)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T04:00:19Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_gemm_nondet_train): cluster split-K FP32 weight gradient on 152-SM GB300 (sm_103a) and 148-SM B200 (#9051)

The dense projection GEMM family ships as a deterministic package,
`flashinfer.cake_dense_gemm_det_train`, and a non-deterministic package,
`flashinfer.cake_dense_gemm_nondet_train`. This PR changes one variant
in the non-deterministic package: the FP32-output K1 weight gradient dW
= G^T X for the thin rows d_in 4096/5120 → d_out 32/48/64/128. This
variant already runs a cluster split-K program on 152-SM GB200
(sm_100a). The program uses 2 or 3 CTAs per cluster and adds their
partial sums through distributed shared memory. This PR brings it to two
more parts.

On 152-SM GB300 (sm_103a), the PR registers the six cluster split-K
programs for sm_103a and uses them in these T windows: 4096 → 32:
1024-32768; 4096 → 48: 1024-6144 and 12288-32768; 4096 → 64: 1024-32768;
4096 → 128: 1024-12288; 5120 → 32: 1024-2048 and 6144-32768; 5120 → 48:
1024-8192; 5120 → 64: 1024-24576; 5120 → 128: 1024-32768. That routes 62
measured rows to the new program, and 7 measured rows stay on the
current route.

On 148-SM B200 (sm_100a), the programs already ship, so the PR only adds
the 148-SM windows: 4096 → 32: 1024-32768; 4096 → 48: 1024-16384 and
32768; 4096 → 64: 1024-6144 and 12288-32768; 4096 → 128: 1024-12288;
5120 → 32, 5120 → 48, 5120 → 64 and 5120 → 128: 1024-32768. That routes
67 measured rows to the new program, and 3 measured rows stay on the
current route.

Over the rows below (62 on GB300, 67 on B200), the new/baseline speedup
ranges are:

- **GB300 op:** 1.035-2.080x (geomean 1.305) vs deterministic Cake and
0.787-1.273x (1.098) vs cuBLAS / cuBLASLt.
- **GB300 training step:** 1.006-1.241x (1.094) and 0.545-1.164x (0.886)
against the same two baselines.
- **GB300 checkpointed step:** 1.005-1.161x (1.066) and 0.475-1.116x
(0.807).
- **B200 op:** 1.041-2.077x (geomean 1.278) vs deterministic Cake and
0.791-1.310x (1.096) vs cuBLAS / cuBLASLt.
- **B200 training step:** 1.011-1.247x (1.086) and 0.544-1.151x (0.897).
- **B200 checkpointed step:** 1.010-1.164x (1.063) and 0.469-1.114x
(0.822).

On GB300, cuBLAS / cuBLASLt is faster than the new route on 18 of 62 op
rows: every row with T ≤ 2048, plus T 4096 on 4096 → 128 and 5120 → 128.
It is also faster on 34 of 62 training-step rows: every T ≤ 6144, plus T
8192 on 4096 → 32, 4096 → 64 and 4096 → 128. In the checkpointed step it
is faster on 38 of 62 rows (every T ≤ 8192).

On B200, cuBLAS / cuBLASLt is faster on 22 of 67 op rows: every row with
T ≤ 4096 except T 4096 on 4096 → 32 and 4096 → 48. It is also faster on
33 of 67 training-step rows: every T ≤ 6144 except T 6144 on 5120 → 32,
plus T 8192 on 4096 → 48 and 4096 → 128. In the checkpointed step it is
faster on 39 of 67 rows (every T ≤ 8192).

All timings below are CUDA-graph replay. With eager launch on GB300, the
deterministic package beats the new route by at most 2.8 % on 10 of 62
training-step rows and 12 of 62 checkpointed-step rows (eager det/new
0.977-1.071 for the step, 0.972-1.054 for the checkpointed step). On
those rows the new route is still faster than the current
non-deterministic route, and in CUDA-graph replay every GB300 row has
det/new ≥ 1.005.

Test systems: NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs) with driver 580.159.03 and
NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs) with driver 580.82.07, both CUDA 13.4
driver API. Both use the CUDA 13.0 runtime (PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130),
kernels JIT-compiled with nvcc 13.4.92, and cuBLAS / cuBLASLt 13.8.0.
Timing: CUPTI GPU span of the call in CUDA-graph replay, cold L2. Each
value is the median over 8 runs per part (2 nodes x 4 runs, arms
interleaved) of the per-run medians. cuBLAS / cuBLASLt is the faster of
torch.mm with FP32 output and the fastest of the first 8 cuBLASLt
heuristic algorithms that meet the same FP32 accuracy budget. Ratios are
baseline / new, so > 1 means the new route is faster.

### [48bb18e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/48bb18ee4c059d711e8ed4f95805d7eda8f90a42)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T03:58:25Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): interleaved tail order for the BF16 runtime-size sink and LSE programs (#9055)

Cake's BF16 paged-context attention (head dim 128; BF16 Q, K, V and
output) ships AOT runtime-size programs `RUNTIME_PACK<p>` at GQA packs
1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12 and 16. Each pack has a plain causal form and
five flag forms: NC, LSE, SINK, NC_LSE and NC_SINK.

The runtime-size causal programs split the causal tail into units. A
per-launch bit selects one of two tail orders: contiguous or
interleaved. The host picks the order for each launch with a makespan
model. Before this PR, only the plain causal programs used the model.
The causal SINK and LSE programs (`RUNTIME_PACK<p>_SINK`,
`RUNTIME_PACK<p>_LSE`) always launched with the contiguous order, even
though their kernels already contained both orders.

This PR lets the causal SINK and LSE programs use the order the model
picks, as the plain causal programs already do. The non-causal programs
are unchanged. When the model keeps the contiguous order, the launch is
identical to before. Control shapes where the order does not change
measured 0.9996x-1.0008x vs the previous version.

On B200, 16 shapes take the interleaved order and run 1.005x-1.231x
faster than the previous version. On GB300, 19 shapes take the
interleaved order and run 1.005x-1.241x faster. No shape is slower.

### [9e0e726](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/9e0e726ffb76aba152e4f1d15564d11d82961349)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T03:40:03Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_gdn): sm_107a gate-stream GDN prefill for FP16 I/O and BF16-state Hq2/Hv8 (up to 1.28x) (#9053)

The Cake GDN prefill family
(`chunk_gated_delta_rule(backend="cake_gdn")`) has 282 prefill variants
with this PR. They differ in I/O data type, state data type, head layout
and fused form (initial state, DV split, gate pipeline, gate stream). A
variant can build for more than one architecture: 115 build for sm_100a,
107 for sm_103a and 139 for sm_107a. This PR adds 16 sm_107a variants of
the full-DV gate-stream prefill that takes an initial state: 8 variants
and an L2-prefetch twin of each. Seven variants and their seven twins
cover FP16 I/O with FP32 state, one per head layout (Hq/Hv 2/8, 4/16,
8/32, 16/16, 16/32, 16/64, 32/32). One variant and its twin cover BF16
I/O with BF16 state for the Hq 2 / Hv 8 head layout. The baseline is the
previous Cake version on FlashInfer `main` (`2eb2e8cb`, which includes
#8982). All 12 measured shapes run the new prefetch twins. Across their
48 seed/mode cells, the geomean speedup is 1.1259x: 1.1014x over the 10
FP16-I/O shapes and 1.2571x over the 2 BF16-state shapes. The largest
speedup is 1.2794x, on BF16 state `397b_tp8_hq2_hv8_128x256`. The
smallest is 1.0128x, on FP16 I/O `x_hq16_hv16_16x512`.

### [01f12ce](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/01f12ce982f8b0e39f4688369afb8601fb950a9e)

- **作者**: shyeh25
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T03:39:44Z
- **提交信息**: perf(trtllm-gen): opt-in wave-fill KV split for decode (FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_GEN_MULTI_WAVE_KV_SPLIT=2) (#8744)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Adds a second value to the opt-in
`FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_GEN_MULTI_WAVE_KV_SPLIT` flag (from #6331) for
trtllm-gen GQA decode.

Under CUDA graphs the KV split is planned from `max_seq_len`, not from
the per-request KV lengths. More splits shorten the longest CTA when
lengths are long and mixed, but add reduction work when they are short
or uniform, and the planner cannot tell the two apart. `=1` keeps its
current rule; `=2` is a more aggressive opt-in for workloads known to
have long, mixed-length KV.

| Flag value | Behavior |
|---|---|
| unset / `0` / any other string | Stock one-wave split (unchanged). |
| `1` | Unchanged (#6331): up to 4 waves when one wave gives at most 2
splits. |
| `2` (new) | When one wave gives 1..15 splits: take the largest split
<= min(16, tuned maximum) within 8 waves and with `ceil(attention window
/ split) >= 4096`, whose waves are at least 4/5 as full as the fullest
candidate's. One-wave splits of 9..15 take the 4-wave split, capped the
same way. Base CTAs above the SM count use the `1` rule; one-wave splits
>= 16 stay stock. |

Notes on `=2`:
- **Wave fill.** A nearly empty last wave costs a full wave when KV
lengths are similar; requiring >= 4/5 of the fullest candidate's fill
avoids such splits. The comparison is done in integers (`5 * s *
slots(f) >= 4 * f * slots(s)`).
- **More than 4 waves is safe here.** #6331 caps waves at 4 because the
separate reduction kernel needs base CTAs <= 2 x SMs. `=2` only applies
when one wave gives at least one split, i.e. base CTAs <= SMs. The
counter bound, INT32 grid check, scratch-fit fallback (a raised split
that does not fit the workspace reruns with the stock split), CGA/GMEM
reselection and tuned-maximum handling are unchanged; no raised split
exceeds 16, so the >16 CGA clamp is not involved.
- **Trade-off.** With a large `max_seq_len` the 4096-token check cannot
see that the real KV is short, so short or uniform KV can be slower than
stock. `=2` stays opt-in and does not change `=0` or `=1`.
- The flag is parsed once per process: exactly `"1"` or `"2"` opt in;
anything else keeps stock (as `getBoolEnv` does today for `"1"`).

**Why a new value instead of changing `=1`.** Neither rule wins
everywhere, so replacing `=1` would slow down some current `=1` users.
`=2` vs `=1`, same cases as the Performance section (36 per GPU, batch
148 excluded, differences within 2% counted as a tie; ranges cover B200
and GB300):

| | `=2` faster | `=1` faster |
|---|---|---|
| `max_seq_len` ≈ real lengths | 15-16 of 36 cases | 4-5 of 36 (by ≤ 7%)
|
| `max_seq_len` 1M | 10-11 of 36 (all long KV, up to 1.53×) | 15 of 36
(12 of them short KV; `=2` down to 0.41× of `=1`) |

Keeping `=1` as is leaves existing users unaffected, and the unset path
is unchanged (see the main vs PR row in Performance).

Files: `include/flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaKernels.cuh`,
`tests/attention/test_trtllm_gen_attention_decode.py`, `CLAUDE.md` (flag
documentation).

## 📊 Performance

Same method as #6331, with a column for the new value.

**Summary.** Speedup = time with the flag unset ÷ time with the value
(above 1 is faster).

| Case | B200 `=1` | B200 `=2` | GB300 `=1` | GB300 `=2` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_seq_len` = `s_kv` (`flashinfer_benchmark.py`): all 42 cases,
geometric mean | 1.004× | 1.059× | 0.990× | 1.035× |
| `max_seq_len` = `s_kv` (`flashinfer_benchmark.py`): long KV (64k,
288k) with random lengths, range over 14 cases | 1.00-1.61× | 1.05-1.66×
| 1.00-1.29× | 1.04-1.33× |
| `max_seq_len` = `s_kv` (`flashinfer_benchmark.py`): short KV (8k),
worst of 14 cases | 0.63× | 0.77× | 0.69× | 0.88× |
| `max_seq_len` 1M under a CUDA graph (as in serving): all 42 cases,
geometric mean | 1.190× | 1.108× | 1.121× | 1.052× |
| `max_seq_len` 1M under a CUDA graph: long KV (64k, 288k) with
lognormal lengths, range over 14 cases | 1.00-2.42× | 1.27-2.68× |
1.00-1.80× | 1.23-1.87× |
| `max_seq_len` 1M under a CUDA graph: short KV (8k) with uniform
lengths, range over 7 cases | 0.57-1.00× | 0.46-0.92× | 0.74-1.00× |
0.41-0.95× |

- `=2` gains most on long KV with mixed lengths, including batches where
`=1` keeps the stock split (batch 16 at 1M, lognormal 64k / 288k: `=2`
1.40× / 1.27× on B200, 1.38× / 1.24× on GB300).
- `=2` loses on short KV with similar lengths under a large
`max_seq_len`: the 4096-token check sees `max_seq_len`, not the real
lengths.
- Flag unset, this PR vs `main` (4c083b49), same 42 cases interleaved on
one GPU, 3 rounds: PR ÷ `main` time is 1.000× on both GPUs and every
case is within 0.995-1.006×, so unset behaviour is unchanged.

**Which value to use**

| Your workload | Use | B200 (148 SMs) | GB300 (152 SMs) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Long KV (≥ 64k), widely varying lengths | `2` | `2` is 1.05-1.66×
faster than unset when `max_seq_len` is close to the longest request,
and 1.27-2.68× faster when `max_seq_len` is 1M. | 1.04-1.33× and
1.23-1.87× faster, same two cases. |
| Short KV (~8k), widely varying lengths, `max_seq_len` much larger than
the real lengths (e.g. CUDA graphs at 1M) | `1` | `1` is 1.39× faster
than unset (geometric mean; 1.00-2.08× per case); `2` 1.04×. | `1` 1.23×
(0.98-2.09×); `2` 0.97×. |
| Anything else, or not sure | unset | Worst case, short KV with similar
lengths at `max_seq_len` 1M: `1` runs at 0.57× and `2` at 0.46× of the
unset speed. | `1` 0.74×, `2` 0.41×. |

- Speedup = time with the flag unset ÷ time with the value; median of 3
rounds.
- This table excludes batch 148 (base CTAs above the SM count; `2` uses
the `1` rule there). The summary above includes all batches.
- Measured lengths: 8k, 64k, 288k only. "Widely varying" = uniform in
[1, `s_kv`] or lognormal with sigma 0.6; "similar" = all equal, or
0.8-1.2× of the mean.
- One shape: 32 Q / 2 KV heads, head dim 128, FP8 KV, q_len 1, page 64.

**Reproducible benchmark.** `benchmarks/flashinfer_benchmark.py`,
routine `BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper`, backend `trtllm-native`:

python benchmarks/flashinfer_benchmark.py --routine
BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper \
--backends trtllm-native --page_size 64 --batch_size 38 --s_qo 1 --s_kv
65536 \
--num_qo_heads 32 --num_kv_heads 2 --head_dim_qk 128 --head_dim_vo 128 \
      --q_dtype fp8_e4m3 --kv_dtype fp8_e4m3 --out_dtype bfloat16 \
      --random_actual_seq_len --num_iters 50 --dry_run_iters 10

Each case runs with `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_GEN_MULTI_WAVE_KV_SPLIT` unset,
`=1` and `=2`, interleaved on the same GPU, three rounds; each value is
the median of the three. The tool sets `max_seq_len` to `--s_kv`;
"fixed" = every KV length is `s_kv`, "random" = uniform in [1, `s_kv`]
(seed 42). Timing is CUPTI with a cold L2 cache. Batches 16, 25, 37, 38,
56, 74, 148; `s_kv` 8k, 64k, 288k. On B200 the unset → `=1` column
reproduces #6331's published numbers (e.g. batch 38, 64k random: 173 →
112 µs vs 173 → 114; batch 25, 8k fixed: 27.3 → 40.9 µs vs 27.5 → 40.7).

The 1M sweep follows #6331's first table: FP8 KV, 32 Q / 2 KV heads,
head dim 128, q_len 1, page 64, `max_seq_len` 1M, a CUDA graph of 10
calls replayed 20 times, timed with CUDA events around each replay (L2
not flushed), per-call median, three rounds. "uniform" = each KV length
0.8-1.2× of the mean; "lognormal" = sigma 0.6 with the same mean.

All numbers are from main 4c083b49 with this PR applied, one GPU per
machine. Round-to-round spread (max − min over median): B200 median 0.1%
(`flashinfer_benchmark.py`) and 0.2% (1M sweep), max 1.4% and 6.3%;
GB300 median 0.1%, max 1.3% and 1.8%.

**How to read the tables below**: one row per batch; each KV length and
length distribution has three columns, the per-call time in µs with the
flag unset, `=1` and `=2`; the number in brackets is the speedup over
unset. Example: batch 25 under 8k fixed reads 27.3, 40.9 (0.67×), 27.3
(1.00×) = every KV length 8k takes 27.3 µs by default, 40.9 µs with `=1`
(slower) and 27.3 µs with `=2` (unchanged).

New `=2` tests (`test_trtllm_batch_decode_wave_fill_kv_split`,
`test_trtllm_batch_decode_wave_fill_flag_values`) run each flag value in
its own subprocess (the flag is read once per process) and check the
exact CTA count from the debug launch log against a Python mirror of the
rule, bitwise equality where the launch must equal stock or `=1`, an
fp32 reference (elementwise tolerance plus a relative-error bound), and
LSE. Cases cover every one-wave split 1..15 and >= 16, base CTAs above
the SM count, the exact 4/5 fill tie and a rejected candidate, the
4096-token window boundary for both branches, a sliding window, eight
waves with the separate reducer (head dim 512), bf16 Q with a binding
tuned maximum, `max_seq_len` above the KV lengths, CUDA graph capture
with a caller-owned counter buffer replayed three times with other
lengths (counters must return to zero), scratch capacity exact / one
byte short (also with LSE and an 8-byte workspace misalignment, and for
the separate reducer), and invalid flag strings. The existing `=1` tests
are unchanged apart from the shared runner taking a flag string and
allowing several launches per case.

Run on B200 (148 SMs) and GB300 (152 SMs) on main 4c083b49: the
multi-wave and wave-fill tests pass (63 passed and 1 skipped on B200,
because no batch gives a one-wave split of 15 on 148 SMs; 64 passed on
GB300). The whole `test_trtllm_gen_attention_decode.py` passes with the
flag unset and with `=2` (B200 1134 passed, GB300 1135 passed); that run
was on e162ed5, whose kernel header and test file are identical to
4c083b49's.

## Reviewer Notes

- `=1` behavior is unchanged; `=2` only runs inside the existing
multi-wave retry path, so every existing fallback still applies.
- The 4/5 threshold, the 8-wave cap and the 4096-token window check are
the knobs a reviewer may want to discuss; the trade-off for short or
uniform KV under a large `max_seq_len` is the main reason `=2` is a
separate opt-in rather than a change to `=1`.
- The trade-off is measured in the Performance section: with
`max_seq_len` 1M, short KV with similar lengths runs at 0.46-0.92×
(B200) and 0.41-0.95× (GB300) of the unset speed with `=2`, while long
KV with lognormal lengths runs at 1.27-2.68× and 1.23-1.87×.
- AI assistance was used.

* **New Features**
* Added an opt-in wave-fill mode for multi-wave KV splitting, selected
with `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_GEN_MULTI_WAVE_KV_SPLIT=2`. For eligible
workloads, it can choose up to 16 splits, subject to KV-window,
workspace, wave-capacity, and minimum per-split size limits.
* The setting is read once per process. Only the exact values `"1"` and
`"2"` opt in; other values retain the stock behavior.
* **Documentation**
* Documented supported values, mode constraints, and cases where
increased splitting may be slower.

### [3bc3b43](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3bc3b4351f1da01d2613f36d429602da9a6c8c17)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T03:30:39Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_mhc_head_nondet_train): add the non-deterministic mHC training head module (#8928) (#9044)

The mHC training head computes `Y = X.mean(dim=1)` over the four
residual streams of a BF16 `X` of shape `[T, 4, H]`. It also computes
the gradient: `dY / 4` goes to each stream, or is added into an existing
`dX` with `accumulate=True`. Cake ships the head in two variants, each
with forward, backward and backward-accumulate kernels on a single rank.
The deterministic variant, `flashinfer.cake_mhc_head_det_train`, has
already shipped. This PR adds the non-deterministic variant,
`flashinfer.cake_mhc_head_nondet_train`, under the name #8928 reserves
for it.

Each forward output is a fixed-order sum of four inputs and the backward
is elementwise, so the new module runs the same kernels as the
deterministic one under its own names. Its outputs are bitwise equal to
the deterministic module's on every measured shape. Against the
deterministic head it is at parity: 0.995x to 1.002x on every
single-call row. Call sequences are 1.00x to 1.01x, except on GB300 at T
= 1024, where host launch gaps add noise (0.95x for forward + backward).
Against torch.compile, the strongest non-Cake baseline measured, single
calls are 0.92x to 1.03x on B200, 0.92x to 1.45x on GB300 (1.45x for
backward accumulate at [4096, 4, 4096]) and 0.89x to 1.02x on R200. The
new module is slower for backward at T = 1024 (0.89x to 0.92x). It is
also 4% to 7% slower on several R200 single-call rows at T 4096 to
65536. Call sequences are 1.64x to 2.21x faster at T = 1024, mostly
because of torch.compile's host dispatch time. At T >= 4096 they are
0.98x to 1.11x on B200, 0.98x to 1.43x on GB300 and 0.94x to 1.03x on
R200.

60.96 | 1.00x | 0.96x |

62.78 | 1.00x | 0.96x |

(checkpointed) | 720.13 | 673.64 | 720.13 | 1.00x | 0.94x |

Latency is the CUPTI GPU time of one call, from the beginning of the
first kernel to the end of the last. L2 is flushed before every call,
launches are eager without CUDA graphs, and each row is the median of at
least 95 calls (CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130). Speedup is baseline
latency divided by non-deterministic Cake latency, so above 1 means the
new module is faster. Deterministic Cake is
`flashinfer.cake_mhc_head_det_train` at FlashInfer main `915eeed2`.
Non-Cake is `torch.compile` (`mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs"`, static
shapes) of the same PyTorch formulas: `X.mean(dim=1)`, the broadcast `dY
/ 4`, and `dX.add_(dY.unsqueeze(1), alpha=0.25)`. PyTorch eager is 1.98x
to 11.7x slower than torch.compile on every single-call row. The one row
where eager was faster shows eager instead and is marked "(eager)".
GB300 rows are the best median of three runs of every implementation,
because torch.compile's autotuned kernel choice changed between compiles
there. For example, backward accumulate at [4096, 4, 4096] measured
65.12, 109.79 and 109.79 us, while Cake's values agreed across runs.
B200 and R200 rows are one run each. The "forward + backward" and "2x
forward + backward (checkpointed)" rows time the whole call sequence,
including host launch gaps between calls. At T = 1024 those gaps
dominate, so torch.compile, with its higher per-call host cost, is
slower there and those rows are noisier.

The other Cake mHC variants are the layer training kernels
`flashinfer.cake_mhc_det_train` and `flashinfer.cake_mhc_nondet_train`
(forward and backward, each split into prepare and finish stages); the
mHC family ships on sm_100a and sm_103a at hidden 4096, 5120 and 7168,
and on sm_107a at hidden 4096.

### [aeb97e7](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/aeb97e7e837e9cad432c3d598f704d353b2ecf94)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T03:18:32Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mok_bf16): two-phase all-thread quantize and next-task prefetch in the sm_107a MXFP8 backward dispatch (#7821) (#9050)

FlashInfer's MoK mixture-of-experts training kernel family covers
forward, full-forward checkpoint recompute and backward. It has four
variants: BF16 or MXFP8 routed experts, each with plain or clamped
SwiGLU.

This PR speeds up the MXFP8 backward kernel on sm_107a (for #7821). It
covers all four sm_107a backward builds: plain or clamped SwiGLU, each
with BF16 or FP32 weight-gradient outputs. The change is in how the
communication CTAs dispatch dy and x as vectors.

Before, each 128-column tile of a 256-column half ran two MXFP8
quantizers on separate threads. The column-major (transposed) quantizer
ran on threads 0-127, and the row-major quantizer ran on threads
128-255. For dy, all threads first scaled the half in place. The row
quantizer then re-read every row it had just written. The two thread
groups did unequal work behind five barriers (four for x).

Now all threads run the quantize in two phases:

- **Phase 1:** each of the 256 threads takes one row of one tile. It
loads the row and, for dy only, scales it and writes it back. It then
quantizes the row to row-major MXFP8 from registers. The row-major
stores leave as one bulk group.
- **Phase 2:** all 256 threads quantize their tile's row pairs
column-major from the scaled values. These stores leave as a second bulk
group.

A buffer is rewritten only after the previous half's matching group has
been read. A half now takes three barriers.

The communication CTAs also prefetch the next task's schedule. The first
128 threads read the next task's peer, token and router weight while the
current task's low half is quantized. Before, they read these right
before each vote or barrier. The router-weight preload for macro batch 0
now unrolls its row loop four times. Every vote and barrier stays.

Every quantized block, scale byte and stored byte is unchanged, so
outputs are bitwise identical. There is no interface, workspace or
memory change. The forward and recompute kernels are unchanged, and so
are the sm_100a and sm_103a kernels. On the measured kernels, backward
SASS shrinks by about 2300 instructions per build (plain: 34000 →
31697).

**Kernel phases** (recompute replay mode, ms)

| Workload | Forward | Recompute replay | Backward |
|---|---|---|---|
| T=27116, uniform routing | 3.894 → 3.948 (0.986x) | 2.762 → 2.791
(0.990x) | 6.621 → 6.380 (1.038x) |
| T=32768, uniform routing | 4.646 → 4.682 (0.992x) | 3.206 → 3.226
(0.994x) | 8.515 → 8.257 (1.031x) |
| T=27116, hot-expert routing 1.25x | 5.744 → 5.763 (0.997x) | 3.125 →
3.134 (0.997x) | 10.296 → 9.951 (1.035x) |
| T=27116, hot-expert routing 2x | 11.119 → 11.185 (0.994x) | 3.124 →
3.141 (0.995x) | 21.259 → 20.822 (1.021x) |

**End to end**, recompute replay (ms)

| Workload | MoE microbatch | Training update (5 layers) |
|---|---|---|
| T=27116, uniform routing | 13.972 → 13.799 (1.013x) | 139.624 →
137.913 (1.012x) |
| T=32768, uniform routing | 17.084 → 16.876 (1.012x) | 170.563 →
168.823 (1.010x) |

→ 196.172 (1.014x) |

359.568 (1.009x) |

update (5 layers) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Forward replay (checkpoint replay re-runs the full forward) | 1 |
11.124 → 11.167 (0.996x) | 21.310 → 20.833 (1.023x) | 44.253 → 43.767
(1.011x) | 441.016 → 437.215 (1.009x) |

– |

*8 NVIDIA VR NVL72 GPUs (sm_107a, 212 SMs, two 4-GPU trays in one NVLink
domain), CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. EP8, H=4096, I=2048, 288
experts, top-8, one shared expert, clamped SwiGLU (limit 10), FP32
weight gradients, MXFP8 routed experts, macro batch 262144 rows.
"Before" has the same MoK kernels as this PR's base (FlashInfer main
with #8988). "After" adds this change, and its backward kernels are
byte-identical to this PR's. Recompute-mode values are the mean of 2
runs per side. The runs were interleaved in mirrored order with other
variants in one job on the same two nodes. Mean SM clocks agree within 4
MHz. The forward and replay kernels are identical on both sides, so
their small slowdowns (up to 0.054 ms) do not come from forward or
replay code. The microbatch and training-update times include these
slowdowns. Peak memory per rank is identical. Outputs, input gradients,
routing-score gradients and weight gradients are bitwise identical to
before on all 8 ranks, with FP32 weight-gradient accumulators seeded
identically.*

The family also ships the BF16 routed-expert variants and the MXFP8
forward and recompute kernels, and every variant runs on sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a; this change applies to the sm_107a MXFP8 backward
only.

### [e609887](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e609887f97b7f4c6c249d9de5008679a495dcfa2)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T02:52:30Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det_train): sm_103a FP8 picks the wide unit by waves of the grid (#9047)

`flashinfer.cake_dsa_indexer_det_train.cake_dsa_indexer_det_train_topk`
is the deterministic DSA indexer top-k. It has two Cake variants: the
default BF16 form and the opt-in FP8 form (`float8_e4m3fn` q / k with a
per-key FP32 `k_scale`). This PR changes only the FP8 form, and only on
sm_103a. Earlier FP8 PRs:

- #8749 added the FP8 form and #8781 improved it.
- #8841 / #8895 / #8933 added an FP8 wide program on sm_103a / sm_100a /
sm_107a.
- #8954 picks the FP8 wide unit by wave count on sm_100a.
- #8976 made the sm_100a FP8 l6 programs load K_scale one tile ahead.
- #8986 added an FP8 l6 snake program on sm_107a for short
single-document calls.
- #9021 runs one-document sm_103a FP8 wide calls in the `:lsf` copy.

The FP8 scan programs split queries into units. Narrow units hold 4
queries, l6 (three-warpgroup) units hold 6 and wide units hold 8. A
unit's waves on the persistent grid are ceil(ceil(T / queries per unit)
/ CTAs), and W = l6 waves / wide waves. For causal documents (key ratio
1), mean unit tiles = (Tkv - T / 2) / segments / 128.

Before this PR, sm_103a FP8 calls in the l6 range (mean unit tiles <=
1024, top-k >= 512) used the l6 program. The exception was calls with at
least 512 mean unit tiles and enough wide rounds. Now the sm_103a FP8
dispatch picks the wide unit by waves of the persistent grid, as sm_100a
already does (#8954). The rule is the record field `wide_wave_rule` =
[1.7, 1.15, 64.0, 2048, 1.1, 112.0, 3.5, 14, 1.26, 40.0, 9.0] in the
sm_103a FP8 record.

The wide unit takes a call from the narrow unit when the narrow units
need at least 1.7 times its waves. It takes a call from the l6 unit when
W >= 1.15 and the mean unit tiles reach a floor:

- The floor is 64 for one document of at least 14 wide waves, plus 3.5
for each wide wave below 14.
- On a packed call (two or more documents), the floor is at least 112.
- While W < 1.26, the floor is at least 40 / (W - 1): 160 at W = 1.25
and 240 at W = 7 / 6. On a packed call it is then also at least 9 / (W -
1) ** 2: 225 at W = 1.2 and 324 at W = 7 / 6.
- Above top-k 2048, the floor grows as (top_k / 2048) ** 1.1.

Below the floor, the l6 unit measured faster, so those calls stay on l6
(J6, PK1 and F5 below). One-document wide calls from 64 mean unit tiles
still use the `:lsf` copy (#9021), and packed calls keep their segment
order. The sm_100a FP8 rule (three elements) and all BF16 records are
unchanged, so their plans do not change.

The baseline is the previous Cake version: the FP8 dispatch on
FlashInfer main before this PR, which includes #9021. Ids and scores are
bit-identical between the two sides on every measured row.

**NVIDIA GB300, sm_103a (152 SMs), CUDA 13.4 (13.4.92), PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130.**

Each time is the CUPTI-measured GPU interval covering every kernel of
one call: scan, merge and finalize of a prepared runner into
caller-owned outputs and workspace. Settings are cold L2, eager launch,
3 warm-up iterations and 20 repetitions. The previous and this-PR arms
run in the same process. Each run's value is the median over three arm
orders (A then B, B then A, interleaved). The tables give the median
over 2 runs, which are separate processes on separate GPUs of one node.
Rows whose program does not change run the same program on both sides,
so they show parity by construction. "vs previous" = previous time /
this PR time (above 1 = faster). An A/A twin of each arm bounds the
noise: a row counts as a speedup only when every run and order exceeds 1
+ the row's A/A band. Every "x" row without "(parity)" in the tables
passed that test.

Owner shapes, all top-k 2048 and causal. P1 is a recorded packed
training call with 8 segments, and s2_4x2k_packed is 4 x 2048 queries
over 18432 / 43008 / 67584 / 100352 keys.

### [fed9283](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/fed928357da59d81dd74144bf6f54aa236d7325b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T02:48:37Z
- **提交信息**: refactor(cake_kda_nondet)!: name the non-deterministic KDA training modules by mode, with the det KCP rename (#8928) (#9017)

## Summary

Part of #8928. Each Cake training name states its mode (`det` / `nondet`), no entry takes `deterministic=`, and backends live under `flashinfer/experimental/cake/<module>/`. This PR renames the remaining packages of the KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) chunked-training family:

- **Non-deterministic, single rank:** `flashinfer.cake_kda_train` → `flashinfer.cake_kda_nondet_train`
- **Non-deterministic, KCP (context parallel):** `flashinfer.cake_kda_train_kcp` → `flashinfer.cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp`
- **Deterministic, KCP:** `flashinfer.cake_kda_det_train_kcp` keeps its module path. Its backend moves under `flashinfer/experimental/cake/`, and its entries and types get names that start with the mode.

## Depends on

#9008 (deterministic single-rank rename) and #8801 (non-deterministic single-rank in-kernel Q/K L2 norm) are merged. This branch merges main after both, so its diff against main holds only this rename. The branch is not rebased. The deterministic KCP commits joined this branch by merge.

## Migration

### Non-deterministic KDA (single rank and KCP)

| Old | New |
| --- | --- |
| module `flashinfer.cake_kda_train` (mode selector, `deterministic=` keyword) | `flashinfer.cake_kda_nondet_train` (stable API, `@flashinfer_api`; backend imported on first use) |
| package `flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_kda_train` | `flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_kda_nondet_train` |
| `chunk_kda` | `cake_kda_nondet` |
| `chunk_kda_fwd` / `chunk_kda_bwd` | `cake_kda_nondet_train_forward` / `cake_kda_nondet_train_backward` |
| `kda_train_arena`, `kda_train_workspace`, `kda_train_workspace_bytes`, `kda_train_saved_bytes` | `cake_kda_nondet_train_arena`, `cake_kda_nondet_train_workspace`, `cake_kda_nondet_train_workspace_bytes`, `cake_kda_nondet_train_saved_bytes` |
| `is_kda_train_supported` | `is_cake_kda_nondet_train_supported` |
| backend `ChunkKDAFunction`, `KdaWorkspace`, `KdaChunkSaved`, `KdaArena` | `CakeKDANondetFunction`, `CakeKDANondetWorkspace`, `CakeKDANondetChunkSaved`, `CakeKDANondetArena` |
| module `flashinfer.cake_kda_train_kcp` | `flashinfer.cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp` (stable API, `@flashinfer_api`) |
| package `flashinfer.experimental.cake_kda_train_kcp` | `flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp` |
| `chunk_kda_kcp` | `cake_kda_nondet_kcp` |
| `chunk_kda_fwd_kcp` / `chunk_kda_bwd_kcp` | `cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp_forward` / `cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp_backward` |
| `partition_kcp`, `build_context_kcp` | `cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp_partition`, `cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp_build_context` |
| `kda_workspace_bytes_kcp`, `kda_saved_bytes_kcp`, `kda_comm_bytes_kcp`, `kda_handoff_bytes_kcp` | `cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp_workspace_bytes`, `cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp_saved_bytes`, `cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp_comm_bytes`, `cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp_handoff_bytes` |
| `reduce_gate_param_grads_kcp`, `kcp_handoff_stats` | `cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp_reduce_gate_param_grads`, `cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp_handoff_stats` |
| `ContextKcp`, `PartitionKcp`, `WorkspaceKcp`, `SavedKcp`, `RecomputeHandleKcp`, `OptionsKcp` | `CakeKDANondetKcpContext`, `CakeKDANondetKcpPartition`, `CakeKDANondetKcpWorkspace`, `CakeKDANondetKcpSaved`, `CakeKDANondetKcpRecomputeHandle`, `CakeKDANondetKcpOptions` |
| backend `ChunkKDAFunctionKcp`, `CallKcp`, `FragmentKcp` | `CakeKDANondetKcpFunction`, `CakeKDANondetKcpCall`, `CakeKDANondetKcpFragment` |

The `__init__` of each non-deterministic backend package no longer re-exports the internal host-plan helpers (`Plan`, `plan`, `is_supported`, `workspace_bytes`, `saved_bytes`, `output_bytes`, `memory_report`, `seg_states_saved`). As in #9008, you can still import them from each package's `cake_backend` module.

### Deterministic KCP

The module `flashinfer.cake_kda_det_train_kcp` keeps its path. Its entries and types get names that start with the mode: `cake_kda_det_kcp`, `cake_kda_det_train_kcp_forward` / `cake_kda_det_train_kcp_backward`, `cake_kda_det_train_kcp_partition` / `cake_kda_det_train_kcp_build_context`, and the `CakeKDADetKcp*` types.

### Backend directories

| Old backend directory | New backend directory | Mode | Dependency |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flashinfer/experimental/cake/cake_kda_train/` | `flashinfer/experimental/cake/cake_kda_nondet_train/` | non-deterministic, single rank | none |
| `flashinfer/experimental/cake_kda_train_kcp/` | `flashinfer/experimental/cake/cake_kda_nondet_train_kcp/` | non-deterministic, context parallel (KCP) | requires sibling `cake_kda_nondet_train` (`build.json` `common.requires.packages`); vendor both |
| `flashinfer/experimental/cake_kda_det_train_kcp/` | `flashinfer/experimental/cake/cake_kda_det_train_kcp/` | deterministic, KCP | requires sibling `cake_kda_det_train` |

Note: `flashinfer/experimental/cake_kda_train/` (one level, without `cake/`) was the deterministic compatibility package that #8908 removed. It never held the non-deterministic package.

## Behavior

- There are no aliases, so the old names fail at import.
- No entry takes `deterministic=`, and passing it raises `TypeError` like any unknown keyword. The old selector default (`deterministic=True` ran the deterministic package) is gone. Callers of the deterministic path import `flashinfer.cake_kda_det_train` / `flashinfer.cake_kda_det_train_kcp`.
- Under `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`, also with `warn_only=True`, the non-deterministic entries run the non-deterministic package and raise no alert or warning. Nothing falls back to the deterministic package.
- Each package refuses a workspace, saved set or arena from the other mode's package with a `ValueError` that names the mode. This applies in both directions.
- The deterministic single-rank package's messages and mode-guard test now use the non-deterministic package's new names.
- No kernel, program, planner rule or build changes. Library stems `cake_kda_train_<20 hex>[_kcp]`, kernel symbols, csrc file names and the `cake_jit` / `cake_kcp_jit` records keep their names. In `build.json` only `"package"` changes, apart from the KCP sibling declaration described below. Internal backend helpers (`plan`, `workspace_bytes`, `saved_bytes`, `kcp_plan`, `KcpPreconditionError`, ...) keep their names.

## Standalone packages

Follows #6553. Each KCP package declares its single-rank sibling in `common.requires.packages` of its `build.json` / `build.test.json`:

- non-deterministic KCP: `["cake_kda_nondet_train"]`
- deterministic KCP: `["cake_kda_det_train"]`

Each KCP package imports that sibling by name from its own parent package (`_single_rank.py`), so a vendored build ships the two directories side by side. In the shared `PACKAGES` table (`scripts/check_cake_build_manifests.py`), these rows carry `requires=`. `tests/cpu/test_cake_packages_standalone.py` imports every backend with `flashinfer` blocked, and the KDA KCP entries are removed from its `ALLOWLIST`.

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [c7f959a](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c7f959a48df1db7eb8839c1ae173c89b4b723a05)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T02:36:36Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_vsa_sm120): split packed plans less once K and V pass 48 MB (#9046)

`BlockSparseAttentionWrapper(backend="vsa_sm120_blk64")` on SM120 /
SM121 has 4 Cake variants: the BF16 and FP16 builds of two persistent
kernels, `vsa_sm120_blk64` (two 128-thread CTAs per SM) and
`vsa_sm120_blk64_pair` (one CTA of two 4-warp groups per SM). Both
kernels run one host plan, and the host planner picks the kernel per
shape. The kernels cover head dim 128, 64 x 64 blocks, GQA and optional
LSE. This PR changes only the host planner, which all 4 variants share.
The kernels, the API and the numerics contract are unchanged. Once the K
and V of all KV heads pass a block limit, the planner charges a split
part a cost of 4 instead of 2. Until now that limit was 2048 blocks (64
MB in 16 bits, half the 128 MB L2 of an RTX PRO 6000) for every plan.
For a plan that may be packed, this PR lowers the limit to 1536 blocks
(48 MB, three eighths of the L2). The packing fills the last partial
wave itself, so splitting every row to fill the virtual CTAs gains less.
Past 48 MB, such a plan now keeps whole rows instead of splitting every
row in two, and the packing then cuts only the rows past the first wave.
Plans that are not packed keep the 2048 limit. Of the 100 measured
shapes, 3 change plan: `h8_n16384_mb48_k32`, `h8_n16384_mb48_k48` and
`h8_n16384_mb48_k64` (3,072 query / 16,384 KV tokens, 8 / 8 heads, top-k
32 / 48 / 64 of 256 KV blocks per query block, BF16, blk64 + packed).
The other 97 keep their plans byte for byte, and their outputs are
bitwise equal to main. On the 3 changed shapes the reduction order
changes, so their outputs differ from main by at most 9.766e-04 (max
abs) and stay within atol = rtol = 1e-2. The baseline is FlashInfer main
at `10979554`, the base of this PR, which runs the previous Cake version
of these kernels and planner. The 3 changed shapes speed up by 1.161,
1.050 and 1.023 with nvcc 13.0 and by 1.162, 1.047 and 1.026 with nvcc
13.4. For example, `h8_n16384_mb48_k32` drops from 115.6 to 99.5 µs with
nvcc 13.0 and from 115.2 to 99.2 µs with nvcc 13.4. Over all 100 shapes,
the geomean speedup is 1.002 with nvcc 13.0 (54 of 100 at or above 1.0,
slowest 0.995) and 1.002 with nvcc 13.4 (52 of 100 at or above 1.0,
slowest 0.996). The geomean is 0.999 (nvcc 13.0) and 1.000 (nvcc 13.4)
on the 22 delivery shapes, 1.000 with both on the 26 held-out shapes,
1.005 with both on the 32 K/V footprint shapes, and 1.002 (nvcc 13.0)
and 1.003 (nvcc 13.4) on the 20 packing boundary shapes.

Measured on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120, 188
SMs, driver 595.84.01) under torch 2.14.1+cu130, with the kernels
JIT-built by CUDA 13.0 and by CUDA 13.4. `wrapper.run` latency is timed
with CUPTI and a cold L2. Each value is the median over 5 interleaved
rounds x 3 input placements. Speedup is main / this PR, so a value above
1 means this PR is faster. The Kernel column names the kernel that this
PR's planner picks for each shape ("blk64" or "pair", with "+ packed"
when the plan packs short KV lists).

### [425f709](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/425f709371893190fc55f3fbb3dcf9498ec9ab40)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T02:13:26Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_dsv4): run the SM107 FP8 64-head ragged 2x257 prefill row on the M64 body (#9027)

Cake's DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA attention for FlashInfer
(`backend="cake"`, `cake_dsv4`) has these variants on FlashInfer main.
On each of sm_100a and sm_103a, 33 BF16/FP8 call forms route to 28
distinct programs (17 BF16, 10 FP8, 1 split reducer). Each of those
targets also has 8 NVFP4 programs, which need CUDA 13.4 or newer. On
sm_107a, the kernel has 10 FP8 programs. The programs cover 8 to 128
query heads. This PR adds no program and changes no kernel. It changes
only the host routing for sm_107a.

This PR delivers one sm_107a row:
- FP8 KV cache, 64 query heads.
- Ragged prefill with 2 requests and max_q_len 257.
- The c4 layer (top-k 4x compressed keys, page size 64), with a sparse
width of 640 per query (128 sliding-window keys + 512 compressed keys).

Before this PR, sm_107a routed this row to a program built only for
sm_100a/sm_103a, so `backend="cake"` raised `ValueError`. With this PR,
the row runs on the sm_107a 64-head M64 multi-tile program. Every
measured call below used its `kv4` form,
`fp8_h64_prefill_source_persistent_m64_multi_tile_kv4`. Routing on
sm_100a and sm_103a does not change. No earlier Cake version serves this
row, so the baseline is FlashInfer's `trtllm-gen` backend on the same
call and inputs at the same FlashInfer commit. Cake's speedup over
`trtllm-gen` on this row is pending on R200 and 1.60x to 1.71x on VR200.

| q_lens | context (tokens/request) | input sets | R200 trtllm-gen (us)
| R200 Cake (us) | R200 speedup | VR200 trtllm-gen (us) | VR200 Cake
(us) | VR200 speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 257, 257 | 4096 | 1 | pending | pending | pending | 32.644 | 20.055 |
1.63x |
| 257, 257 | 16384 | 1 | pending | pending | pending | 32.746 | 20.168 |
1.62x |
| 257, 100 | 4096 | 1 | pending | pending | pending | 25.135 | 14.673 |
1.71x |
| 257, 100 | 16384 | 1 | pending | pending | pending | 25.132 | 14.795 |
1.70x |
| 257, 257 | 4096 | 8 | pending | pending | pending | 33.583 | 20.944 |
1.60x |
| 257, 257 | 16384 | 8 | pending | pending | pending | 33.941 | 21.220 |
1.60x |
| 257, 100 | 4096 | 8 | pending | pending | pending | 25.982 | 15.277 |
1.70x |
| 257, 100 | 16384 | 8 | pending | pending | pending | 26.351 | 15.636 |
1.69x |

GPUs: NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a, 216 SMs) and NVIDIA VR200 (sm_107a, 212
SMs). Software: CUDA 13.4 (nvcc 13.4.92) and PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. Times
are microseconds per call, and speedup = `trtllm-gen` / Cake. q_lens are
the query lengths of each request, and context is the KV tokens per
request. Every query attends all 640 keys. Each call is one of 8
back-to-back calls with PDL, captured in one CUDA graph. With 1 input
set, all 8 calls read the same inputs. With 8 input sets, each call
reads its own inputs. A 512 MiB buffer is zeroed before each graph
replay to flush L2, and per-call time is replay time / 8. Each value is
the median over 16 processes of each process's median over 100 replays,
after 20 warm-up replays.

This PR leaves the kernel's other Cake programs as they are: BF16 and
FP8 on sm_100a and sm_103a, NVFP4 on those targets with CUDA 13.4 or
newer, and the other FP8 programs on sm_107a. `backend="cake"` ships on
sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a, and sm_107a has FP8 only.

### [e9c51ff](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e9c51ff2dee49da7ca7053a6c75fd8e35c7e107e)

- **作者**: burak-inherent
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T01:56:06Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_kda): transpose the BT16 chunk inverse as a 16x16 matrix and compose its off-diagonal block from the complete 8x8 inverses (#6132)

Fixes https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/6130

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`recurrent_kda(backend="cake")` takes the BT16 prepare/chain route for a
compact BF16 state with few sequences (and for an indexed FP32 state
pool). Under slow decay its output and final state are about 15% off an
FP64 recurrence; with keys that share a direction and beta near 1 they
go non-finite. The direct M128 route stays within 0.6% on the same
inputs. Both come from the BT16 prepare kernel's construction of the
16x16 chunk inverse `T = (I + L)^-1`, which it folds into the chain's
factors as `beta * T^T`. The fix is in the three prepare bodies: the
generated `flashkda_generated_bf16_bt16_prepare_0d8e6c8011.cu` and the
hand-written `cake_flashkda_bf16_bt16_prepare.cu` and
`cake_flashkda_bf16_bt16_prepare_beta_tma.cu`, which share the code.

**1. The fold misplaces T's off-diagonal block.** The fold is transposed
with one `movmatrix.trans` per 8x8 block of the fragment, in place. A
16x16 transpose also swaps the two off-diagonal blocks, so `T[8:16,
0:8]` lands at `(1, 0)` of `beta * T^T` instead of `(0, 1)`, and is
scaled by the wrong rows' beta. Rows 0-7 of W and QK lose their
cross-block terms and rows 8-15 gain spurious ones. Those entries couple
tokens on either side of a chunk's midpoint through `Γ_i / Γ_j`, so fast
gates hide the error and slow ones expose it. This is the 15%. The fix
reads the source word as `inverse_frag[(w >> 1) | ((w & 1) << 1)]`, the
same "transpose quadrants, swap off-diagonals" the CuTe DSL prep kernel
in `kda_chunked_bt16.py` does.

**2. The off-diagonal block uses stale diagonal inverses.** `T[8:16,
0:8] = -B22^-1 A21 B11^-1` is composed from `binv_frag`, which is copied
from `diagonal_frag` before the last squaring step writes back, so it
holds `(I - L)(I + L^2)` instead of `(I - L)(I + L^2)(I + L^4)`. The
missing `L^4` terms are negligible for isotropic keys but not when
`beta_i beta_j <k_i, k_j>` is near 1. This is the BT16 form of the stale
fragment #5659 fixed in the M128 bodies, and it is what makes the route
non-finite under the trained-gate statistics of
`test_kda_prefill_trained_gate_distribution.py`. The fix repacks
`diagonal_frag` from the final diagonal values before `binv_frag` is
built, as #5659 does.

**How it was found.**
- In FP64 arithmetic on CPU, the BT16 factorization with the as-built
fold gives 14.2% state / 14.2% output error on the slow-decay input
below; with the correct fold, 0. So the error is structural, not
rounding. With the stale inverses, trained-gate inputs overflow; with
the complete ones, 0.
- On a B300, the `W` factor the prepare kernel writes matches the
as-built fold to 0.29% (BF16 level) and misses the correct one by 13.6%.
- Each fix alone, then both, on a B300 (relative L2 error against the
FP64 recurrence; state / output):

| Input | main | fold swap only | repack only | both | direct M128 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| isotropic, slow decay (`A_log` 0, `dt_bias` -8), 1x512, H12 | 14.75% /
14.61% | 0.46% / 0.54% | 14.75% / 14.61% | 0.46% / 0.54% | 0.52% / 0.59%
|
| trained-gate statistics, 1x512, H12 | non-finite | non-finite | 15.90%
/ 16.20% | 0.32% / 0.37% | 0.33% / 0.39% |
| trained-gate statistics, 1x2048, H12 | non-finite | non-finite |
16.86% / 12.25% | 0.35% / 0.37% | 0.36% / 0.39% |
| isotropic, fast decay, 1x512, H12 | 0.28% / 0.60% | 0.28% / 0.47% |
0.28% / 0.60% | 0.28% / 0.47% | 0.37% / 0.47% |

The hand-written `bt16_prepare` (generated selector made to miss) gives
the same numbers. The hand-written `bt16_prepare_beta_tma` (forced, H16,
1x512) goes from 14.87% / 14.37% (slow decay) and non-finite
(trained-gate statistics) to 0.47% / 0.54% and 0.35% / 0.39%.

**Speed.** No measurable change. Eight shapes FlashInfer's policy sends
to BT16, B300, one GPU, each call captured in a CUDA graph and replayed
300 times with a CUDA event per replay, builds interleaved main / fixed
/ main / fixed, SM clock 2,032 MHz throughout. Median µs per call:

| Shape | Kernels | main | fixed | main | fixed |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| H12, 1x512 | generated prepare + s8 chain | 30.7 | 30.7 | 30.7 | 30.7
|
| H12, 1x2048 | generated prepare + s8 chain | 84.0 | 84.0 | 84.0 | 84.0
|
| H12, 1x8192 | generated prepare + s8 chain | 301.1 | 301.1 | 301.1 |
301.1 |
| H12, 1x16384 | generated prepare + s8 chain | 577.5 | 577.5 | 577.5 |
577.5 |
| H12, 4x4096 | generated prepare + s8 chain | 223.2 | 223.2 | 223.2 |
223.2 |
| H12, 8-sequence varlen, 16,640 tokens | `bt16_prepare` + s7 chain |
223.2 | 223.2 | 223.2 | 223.2 |
| H32, 1x4096 | generated prepare + s8 chain | 186.3 | 185.3 | 185.4 |
186.2 |
| H60, 1x8192 (dense wavefront) | generated prepare + s8 chain | 413.7 |
414.6 | 414.7 | 414.0 |

**Fuzz.** 400 seeded calls with the route forced to BT16 (the policy
picks BT16 on 89 of them), on both builds, against the FP64 recurrence,
with the direct route on an indexed pool as a second opinion. Seeds vary
heads (1-64), fixed and varlen layouts (1-8 sequences, 2-4,096 tokens,
mostly not multiples of 16), gates from fast to very slow plus the
trained-gate statistics, `lower_bound`, `scale`, beta-logit range,
isotropic or direction-sharing q/k, and the initial state. Error is the
larger of state and output relative L2. With `lower_bound` -5, -2.5 or
-1 (312 seeds):

| Route | median | p90 | p99 | max | non-finite | over 1% |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| BT16, main | 12.45% | 58.6% | non-finite | non-finite | 15 | 277 |
| BT16, this PR | 0.50% | 0.65% | 1.06% | 1.26% | 0 | 4 |
| direct M128 | 0.53% | 0.72% | 1.17% | 1.71% | 0 | 9 |

BT16 over direct per seed: median 0.94, max 1.14; the four BT16 seeds
over 1% are long slow or trained-gate rows where direct is also over 1%.
With `lower_bound=-10` (88 seeds) both routes go non-finite on many
seeds (BT16 on 29, direct M128 on 66, BT16 never where direct is
finite), unchanged by this PR; it looks like the in-chunk `k / Γ` factor
leaving FP32 range at up to 10 nats of decay per token, which is outside
this PR. Calls with `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=False`,
`use_gate_in_kernel=False` or `lower_bound=None` are not eligible for
this backend and never launched BT16.

**Generated body.** `flashkda_generated_bf16_bt16_prepare_0d8e6c8011.cu`
is generator output, edited here as #5659 edited its bodies; the
generator needs the same two changes. Since #5919 the JIT/AOT idents are
content-derived, so no metadata changes and the first run rebuilds the
three prepare modules.

## 🔍 Related Issues

- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/6130
- #5659 (the same stale-fragment defect in the M128 bodies; its
description notes BT16 was left untouched).
- #5979 xfails `h12_t512_bt16` as non-finite under trained-gate

- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_gemm_det_train): sm_107a three-chain fp32 weight gradients and ragged weight-gradient rules (#9043)

The Cake deterministic dense GEMM for training
(`flashinfer.cake_dense_gemm_det_train`) has two kernels. K1 is the BF16
dense projection GEMM, with forward, dgrad and wgrad passes and BF16 or
FP32 weight-gradient output. K2 is the FP32 router GEMM, which uses
split-BF16x3. This PR changes only the K1 weight gradient on the 212-SM
and 216-SM `sm_107a` parts. It adds two programs that cut each tile's K
blocks into three chains, which the epilogue sums in order. It also
routes the 4096→512, 4096→1024, 5120→512 and 5120→1024 weight-gradient
rows to new plans. The baseline is the previous Cake version on main,
and speedup is previous / this PR. Across all 100 cells, the speedup
ranges from 1.0497x to 3.1250x, and every row is faster on both parts.
The 208-SM parts keep their plans.

212 SMs, CUDA 13.4. Each pass runs the previous version and this PR
together in one process. Speedup is the pooled ratio over those paired

### [1bb5fa2](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/1bb5fa282fc6f7871119372227fb34aab16a57fa)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T01:47:36Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mhc_det): with grad, L2 hints for fn partial sums above 8192 tokens and mapping-pass tuning on sm_100a (#9042)

FlashInfer's Cake deterministic mHC backend holds the four-stream mHC
kernels with grad. It has forward prepare / recompute and gradient
routes at hidden sizes 4096, 5120 and 7168, group-row forms above 14927
tokens, the dual-layout fn split and the mapping-pass forms. This PR
adds two launch tables on sm_100a at hidden 4096. A private keyword keys
each table by call path, and the public API is unchanged. First, on the
gradient route for 8192 < T ≤ 15590 and 16132 < T ≤ 16263, the slab and
reduction kernels now use the existing L2-hint forms. The slab kernel
stores the fn-gradient partial sums with EVICT_LAST, and the reduction
kernel loads them with EVICT_FIRST. Before this PR, these forms ran only
up to T = 8192. This range adds two new group-row reduction forms. The
activation-checkpoint route keeps the previous forms above 8192. Second,
on the activation-checkpoint route only, the mapping pass now uses the
existing `_xn` forms (X hinted) for 7168 < T ≤ 7680. The forward route
still uses them only up to 7168. sm_103a and sm_107a are unchanged.
Outputs and gradients are bitwise identical to the previous version and
deterministic run to run. The baseline, "previous", is the current Cake
deterministic backend in FlashInfer main. On the six backward rows that
run changed kernels, this PR is 1.002x to 1.004x faster than previous.

**NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, 148 SMs; CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.**
Latency is CUPTI active time per call in microseconds. L2 is flushed
before every call. Every shape uses 4 streams, hidden 4096 and T tokens.
"Checkpoint" is the activation-checkpoint recompute followed by the
gradient route. Each value is the mean of the valid reads from two
record sessions on separate nodes. Each session interleaves three arms
in 6 ABC/CBA groups of 32 iterations: A is previous, B is this PR and C
is a second previous run. A read is valid when the identical-program
control C/A is within 0.99-1.01. Speedup = previous / this PR, and a
value above 1 means this PR is faster. Only backward at T = 14928,
15288, 15566, 15590, 16164 and 16263 runs changed kernels. No row falls
in 7168 < T ≤ 7680, so the checkpoint change has no row. Every other
cell runs the same kernels on both sides, so its ratio shows run-to-run
variation. A 4-arm placement probe ran in the same allocation on every
such cell that read > 1.01 or had a void control. It runs previous, this
PR, previous and this PR for 6 rounds and reports this PR / previous as
(B+D)/(A+C). It read ≤ 1.0035 on every probed cell.

### [272ec9c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/272ec9c8e3964ec1103c043e2a9228a246a2b5cb)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T01:41:06Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda): owner/helper hybrid build of the BF16 KDA prefill M64 module for equal-length 2048+ token launches on GB300 (sm_103a) (#9040)

The Cake chunked KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) prefill behind
`flashinfer.recurrent_kda(..., backend="cake")` has modules with BF16
inputs and modules with TF32 inputs. Both come in fused and split forms.
On GB300, the BF16-input fused M64 module runs the launches that the
pair-share rule takes with the pair-share program. This PR adds an
owner/helper hybrid build of that module for sm_103a (GB300). The new
build uses a (tasks, 3) grid, so each task has one helper CTA and two
owner CTAs, one for each value half. The helper prepares the chunks with
c % 4 >= 2. The owners prepare the other chunks and copy the helper's
packets from a global ring. The new build produces the same bits as the
pair-share program. On GB300, a launch uses the new build when three
conditions hold: the pair-share rule takes it, all sequences have the
same length of 2048 tokens or more, and it has 37 to 50 tasks. This is
row (50, 2048, 1) of the GB300 owner/helper table. Every other launch
keeps its current build. Outputs, final states and checkpoints are
bitwise identical to FlashInfer main. The tables compare this PR with
FlashInfer main on GB300 and report the latency per call in
microseconds. Each table has 56 rows: 12 or 16 heads, no gate lower
bound or -5, and 14 sequence-length shapes. One table covers the
plan-cache fast path, and the other covers the serving pattern. TIE
means no difference beyond the measurement band. Each table has one
faster row, with 12 heads, gate lower bound -5 and shape 4x4096. On the
fast path, the latency goes from 179.71 to 165.47 us (1.09x) on node 1
and from 179.01 to 165.60 us (1.08x) on node 2. In the serving pattern,
it goes from 179.23 to 166.61 us on node 1 and from 180.26 to 166.14 us
on node 2 (1.08x on both). Every other row is TIE, and none is slower.
One fast-path row (16 heads, gate lower bound -5, 2x(8128+64)) has a
dagger. Its A/A drift guard tripped on both nodes, so the table shows it
but does not count it. This PR does not route that launch because its
sequence lengths differ, and its program is byte-identical. On the fast
path, the speedup over the 55 counted rows is 1.00x to 1.09x on node 1
and 1.00x to 1.08x on node 2. In the serving pattern, it is 1.00x to
1.08x over 56 rows on both nodes. We measured against FlashInfer main
before #8994 and #9012 merged. #8994 changed only sm_100a. #9012 changed
two GB300 rows with 16 heads and gate lower bound -5: BS16 x T64 and
BS64 x T64 now run at about 22.30 and 60.83 us on main. This PR does not
change the programs for those rows, so their TIE results still hold, but
their absolute values in the tables come from before #9012. We also
re-measured the shipped program on GB300 nodes over 301 launch shapes.
No shape is slower, and the latency ratio (this PR / main) is 0.88 to
1.00. The tables have GB300 columns only because sm_100a (B200) does not
change: the new build is not built for sm_100a, and every sm_100a
program is byte-identical to FlashInfer main. The other Cake variants
(the TF32-input modules, the split forms and every other program) are
unchanged on both sm_100a and sm_103a.

GB300: NVIDIA GB300, sm_103a, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03. CUDA 13.4
(nvcc), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. B200 (sm_100a): unchanged by this PR
(every program byte-identical).

### [ffd9eb6](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ffd9eb63d22a26ad332b86da7ffad5949d4d3ab9)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T01:38:24Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_kda): with grad, in-kernel Q/K L2 norm in the non-deterministic single-rank and context-parallel packages (#8801)

Cake KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) chunked training kernels come in
deterministic and non-deterministic (ND) packages, each with a
single-rank and a KCP context-parallel version. Each version supports a
precomputed (`g`) or raw (in-kernel) forget gate and an optional
in-kernel Q/K L2 norm. Inputs are bf16 q/k/v with K = V = 128.

This PR delivers `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True` for the ND single-rank
package (`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_kda_train`) and the ND KCP
package (`flashinfer.experimental.cake_kda_train_kcp`). It works in `g`
and raw mode on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a. Before this PR, both
packages raised `ValueError` for this option. The deterministic packages
are unchanged. On all five GPUs, no row is slower than the deterministic
packages in both build orders. In measured cells with the L2 norm on, ND
is 2.03x-6.48x faster than FLA on B200, 2.08x-6.70x on GB200,
1.93x-6.54x on B300, 2.04x-6.77x on GB300 and 1.86x-9.30x on VR200.

Against the ND package on main before this PR, raw-gate bwd and ckpt
with the L2 norm off are about 2% slower (B300 geomean 1.022 bwd / 1.017
ckpt), due to the deterministic accuracy fix #8909 (the ND raw path runs
the deterministic raw programs; det slows by the same amount) and a
fixed reduction order in that path; det/ND is not affected.

### Baselines and timing

- **det**: the deterministic Cake packages, which already support this
option. Single-rank rows: FlashInfer main 29150ffd (since then only its
backend host Python changed, not its kernels). KCP rows: FlashInfer main
07fa3013, which includes the deterministic KCP host prologue change.
- **FLA**: flash-linear-attention `chunk_kda` 0.6.0 with
`use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True`, the strongest non-Cake KDA
implementation with an in-kernel Q/K L2 norm; n/a on KCP rows (a
per-rank shard is not comparable) and with the L2 norm off.
- CUPTI timing with cold L2. Each cell is fwd / bwd / ckpt, where ckpt
is one activation-checkpointed training step (2x forward + backward).
- det/ND and FLA/ND are latency ratios; above 1 means ND is faster. Both
build orders are measured against an A/A noise band. A row counts as
faster or slower only when det/ND is outside the band in both orders.
- The per-GPU tables compare only within a GPU: the round statistic
(median, mean or geomean) and the noise band differ by GPU.

| GPU | arch | rows | faster / parity / outside the band in one order
only / slower | single-rank det/ND geomean | KCP det/ND geomean | FLA/ND
(l2n on, measured cells) |

The per-GPU tables show the delivered variant (in-kernel L2 norm on).
Shapes: P1 = T 239718, 3 docs, H 4; P8 = T 261393, 4 docs, H 4; P12 /
P13 / P14 = P8 with H 16 / 32 / 64; 1 doc and 4 docs at T 16384, H 64;
miles = T 8192 / 16384 / 32768, 1 doc or 4 equal docs, H 12 / 24 / 48;
KCP = T 261392, 4 docs, CP2 or CP4, contiguous or zigzag layout, H 4 /
16 / 64. Rows with the L2 norm off and per-operation verdicts are posted
as one PR comment per GPU.

separate process) x (det@29150ffd / ND, timed in one process). So in 10
KCP rows, det latency / ND latency and det/ND fall on different sides of
1. Row miles T16384 4 docs H48 raw bwd (single-rank, L2 norm off) was
re-measured alone and reads parity.

### [be2c1dc](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/be2c1dccee2b73f0b6dd0dcd1bc20f855491602f)

- **作者**: Vincent
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T01:26:25Z
- **提交信息**: feat(batch_invariant): batch-invariant attention behind `batch_invariant=True` on the paged decode, paged prefill and ragged prefill wrappers (#8590)

## 📌 Description

This PR adds the batch-invariant attention class to the mode introduced
by #8361: a keyword-only `batch_invariant: bool = False` on
`BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper`,
`BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper` and
`BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper`, backed by the new package
`flashinfer/attention/batch_invariant/` (CuTe-DSL kernels generated by
the `flashinfer/batch_invariant` engine).

**Why.** RL training needs the policy's log-probs from training-time
prefill to match the rollout engine's decode bit for bit, and a
request's attention output must not depend on which other requests share
its batch. The default attention backends are batch-variant: FA2 splits
KV by a batch-dependent rule unless pinned (`fixed_split_size`), the
CuTe-DSL decode kernel picks `kv_splits` from the batch and the SM count
and reduces atomically, and prefill and decode run different kernels
with different reduction orders, so the same token gives different bits
on the two paths.

**What the flag guarantees.** With `batch_invariant=True` a token's
output bits depend on its KV position, its head, the window and the
input values alone:

| | Property | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | Run-to-run determinism | same inputs: same bits, across
processes, streams and CUDA-graph replay |
| R2 | Batch invariance | a request's bits do not depend on the batch
size, its neighbours, its position, the page table or the SM count |
| R3 | Configuration agreement | every configuration (ring depth, unit
kind, softmax warpgroups, fold placement, kernel body) gives the same
bits |
| R4 | Cross-path agreement | **prefill == decode** for the same token,
and the paged and ragged KV layouts give the same bits |

One class per head dim (`attention.bf16`, fingerprints
`attn-bf16-d64-9a05233ec9351b0d`, `d128-027b0379515b82e2`,
`d256-b8cb59dab4eb6c0f`): 128-key tiles and 512-key chunks on the
absolute KV axis, an online softmax whose rescale is exactly 1.0 when
the row maximum does not move, a fixed chunk-merge order,
`ex2.approx.ftz` and `max.f32` as the only opaque scalar primitives. The
split-KV kernel's merge is the same fold whether it runs in the fixup
kernel or in the last-arriving CTA. `lean/BIKernels/Attention.lean`
proves R1-R4 on the per-row dataflow (split kernel == fused fold for any
chunk-to-CTA assignment, prefill == decode, the launch model, config
invariance over the enumerated spaces); the generated `Cases.lean`
reproduces the Python spec's terms node for node.

**Kernels.** Three CuTe-DSL bodies compute the class: a
CUTLASS-FMHA-derived row body (prefill and wide units; at D = 64 two Q
tiles per CTA, one per softmax warpgroup), a Swaps-AB decode body (keys
on the MMA M dimension, two ping-pong softmax warpgroups) for units of
at most 8 rows, and a split-KV fixup under programmatic dependent
launch. The ragged wrapper runs the same kernels through a ragged TMA
producer (a 128-token box along the packed token axis), so paged ==
ragged by construction.

**Supported:** bf16 q / K / V / out; head dims 64, 128, 256; GQA
(`num_qo_heads` a multiple of `num_kv_heads`, up to 128 per group);
causal (bottom-right aligned) with an optional `window_left`; page sizes
1..128 (powers of two); NHD / HND; CUDA graphs; SM100, SM103, SM107.
Everything else (soft cap, custom masks, fused RoPE, non-causal prefill,
fp8 / fp4 KV, q / k / v scales, LSE output, sinks) raises
`BatchInvariantUnsupportedError`; nothing falls back.

### Performance

Ratio of the best non-invariant FlashInfer backend's time to ours (FA2 /
cuDNN / trtllm-gen / cute-dsl / Prims TS, the best per point); > 1.0
means the batch-invariant kernel is faster. Cold-L2 CUDA-graph replay,
bf16, 32:8 / 8:8 / 64:8 heads, page 16 / 32. Geomeans:

| part | decode D=64 | decode D=128 | decode D=256 | prefill D=64 |
prefill D=128 | prefill D=256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GB200 (SM100) | 0.82 | 0.90 | 0.87 | 0.71 | 0.69 | 0.66 |
| GB300 (SM103) | 0.81 | 0.89 | 0.91 | 0.65 | 0.65 | 0.60 |

Decode at batch >= 64 is 0.92-0.96 on both parts; batch 1 at short
contexts is the weakest regime (one 512-key chunk per unit).

## 🔍 Related Issues

Follows #8361 (the mode and `mm_bf16(batch_invariant=True)`).

### [02dfb1d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/02dfb1d06b21922bea816d0a9f4f74325c3e676f)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T01:25:27Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det_train): sm_103a FP8 runs one-document wide calls in the :lsf copy (#9021)

`flashinfer.cake_dsa_indexer_det_train.cake_dsa_indexer_det_train_topk`
is the deterministic DSA indexer top-k. It has two Cake variants: the
default BF16 form and the opt-in FP8 form (`float8_e4m3fn` q / k with a
per-key FP32 `k_scale`). This PR changes only the FP8 form, and only on
sm_103a. Earlier FP8 PRs:

- #8749 added the FP8 form and #8781 improved it.
- #8841 / #8895 / #8933 added an FP8 wide program on sm_103a / sm_100a /
sm_107a.
- #8954 picks the FP8 wide unit by wave count on sm_100a.
- #8976 made the sm_100a FP8 l6 programs load K_scale one tile ahead.
- #8986 added an FP8 l6 snake program on sm_107a for short
single-document calls.

On sm_103a, the FP8 wide program (8 queries per unit) has a
longest-first copy (`:lsf`). The dispatch already uses it for packed
calls of unequal documents. On a one-document call, the copy walks the
same units in the same order as the plain program and returns
bit-identical ids and scores, but it measured faster on long units. The
sm_103a FP8 dispatch now runs the copy on one-document calls of the wide
unit from 64 mean unit tiles on. For a causal document (key ratio 1),
mean unit tiles = (Tkv - T / 2) / 128. Every other call keeps its
previous program. The rule is the record field `lsf_single_rule` =
[64.0] in the sm_103a FP8 record (None everywhere else), and only the
FP8 dispatch reads it. The baseline is the previous Cake version: the
FP8 dispatch on FlashInfer main before this PR, which runs the plain
wide program on the rows this PR moves. Ids and scores are bit-identical
between the two sides on every measured row.

**NVIDIA GB300, sm_103a (152 SMs), CUDA 13.4 (13.4.92), PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130.**

Each time is the CUPTI-measured GPU interval covering every kernel of
one call: scan, merge and finalize of a prepared runner into
caller-owned outputs and workspace. Settings are cold L2, eager launch,
3 warm-up iterations and 20 repetitions. The previous and this-PR arms
run in the same process. Each run's value is the median over three arm
orders (A then B, B then A, interleaved). The tables give the median
over 2 runs, which are separate processes on separate GPUs of one node.
Rows whose program does not change run the same program on both sides,
so they show parity by construction. "vs previous" = previous time /
this PR time (above 1 = faster). An A/A twin of each arm bounds the
noise: a row counts as a speedup only when every run and order exceeds 1
+ the row's A/A band.

Owner shapes, all top-k 2048 and causal. P1 is a recorded packed
training call with 8 segments, and s2_4x2k_packed is 4 x 2048 queries
over 18432 / 43008 / 67584 / 100352 keys.

| Shape | Queries T | Keys Tkv | Segments | Program after this PR |
Previous Cake FP8 (ms) | This PR (ms) | vs previous |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| P1 | 16231 | 268757 | 8 | l6, longest-first (unchanged) | 3.1821 |
3.1808 | 1.000x (parity) |
| glm2k_16k | 2048 | 16384 | 1 | l6 (unchanged) | 0.3190 | 0.3201 |
0.997x (parity) |
| s1_8k_on_64k | 8192 | 73728 | 1 | wide, `:lsf` copy (544 mean unit
tiles) | 2.8087 | 2.7880 | 1.007x (per-order 1.0067 to 1.0084, A/A band
0.0017) |
| s2_4x2k_packed | 8192 | 229376 | 4 | l6, longest-first (unchanged) |
2.7053 | 2.7061 | 1.000x (parity) |
| s3_cold16k | 16384 | 16384 | 1 | l6 (unchanged) | 1.1751 | 1.1762 |
0.999x (parity) |

Other one-document calls this PR moves from the plain wide program to
the `:lsf` copy (same GPU and method):

| Queries T | Keys Tkv | top-k | Mean unit tiles | Previous Cake FP8
(ms) | This PR (ms) | vs previous |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 8192 | 12288 | 256 | 64 | 0.4871 | 0.4869 | 1.000x (parity) |
| 8192 | 16384 | 256 | 96 | 0.6341 | 0.6314 | 1.004x (parity: per-order
1.0018 to 1.0070, A/A band 0.0039) |
| 10240 | 20480 | 256 | 120 | 0.9383 | 0.9345 | 1.004x |
| 65536 | 65536 | 256 | 256 | 10.1105 | 10.0722 | 1.004x |
| 131072 | 131072 | 2048 | 512 | 39.8784 | 39.7693 | 1.003x (parity: A/A
band 0.0028) |
| 262144 | 262144 | 2048 | 1024 | 156.9552 | 152.0418 | 1.032x |

Below 64 mean unit tiles, the copy measured slower when forced on this
GPU: 0.985x at 712 queries over 4096 keys (top-k 256, 29 mean unit
tiles) and 0.986x at 2048 queries over 8192 keys (top-k 256, 56 mean
unit tiles), so those calls keep the plain program; for example, 8192
queries over 11264 keys (top-k 256, 56 mean unit tiles) runs the same
program on both sides, at 0.4527 ms before and 0.4548 ms after.

The default BF16 form is unchanged; both Cake forms ship on sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a, and the FP8 form has a wide program on all three
and an l6 snake program on sm_107a.

### [37f3575](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/37f3575b3da07c20c7923cedda1c1c11d2e78c0e)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-07T01:25:12Z
- **提交信息**: refactor(cake_gdn): rename the GDN autograd modules to det / nondet (#8928) (#8959)

> **Validation in progress.** This branch contains both halves of the
rename (nondet and det), including the det update that declares the KCP
option keywords in the entry signatures. GPU validation of this head is
running; the Validation table is filled in when it completes. Until
then, do not merge.

## Description

The GDN training modules now carry their mode in the module and function
names, as #8928 requires for every Cake training family. This PR covers
both modes.

- **Four public modules.** `flashinfer.cake_gdn_nondet_train`,
`flashinfer.cake_gdn_nondet_train_kcp`, `flashinfer.cake_gdn_det_train`
and `flashinfer.cake_gdn_det_train_kcp`. Each one is a stable API
facade: it uses `@flashinfer_api`, has no experimental decorator, emits
no `ExperimentalWarning` and imports its backend lazily. The
`flashinfer` top level binds the four modules lazily through
module-valued `_LAZY_EXPORTS` rows, for example `"cake_gdn_det_train":
(".cake_gdn_det_train", None)`.
- **Backends move as whole directories** to
`flashinfer/experimental/cake/<module>/`. `cake_build.py` and `csrc/**`
(including `csrc/cake_ffi_checks.h`) move unchanged. The `csrc` moves
are pure renames: 126 <!-- RECOUNT --> R100 entries for nondet and 127
<!-- RECOUNT --> for det. In `build.json`, only `"package"` changes. The
two KCP packages also have a `build.test.json`, and only its `"package"`
field changes. The single-rank packages have no `build.test.json`.
`cake_jit.PACKAGE` also changes. `LIBRARY_PREFIX`, library names,
program names and `csrc` file names stay the same.
- **Only the name sets the mode.** No entry, forwarded backend entry or
autograd `Function.forward`/`backward` takes `deterministic`. Passing
`deterministic=` raises `TypeError`. Entries that accept option keywords
(`**knobs`/`**kw`) reject it when called. No environment variable
selects a mode.
- **Tapes record the mode.** The non-deterministic single-rank forward
tape records `"mode": "nondet"`. Its backward raises `ValueError` for a
tape without that tag. The deterministic single-rank tape will record
`"mode": "det"`. Its backward will refuse a tape of the other mode.
<!-- VERIFY det tape tag at final head -->
- **No aliases.** Old module paths raise `ModuleNotFoundError`. Old
names raise `ImportError`/`AttributeError`.
- **Kernels, programs and numerics are unchanged.** A bitwise A/B test
compared the single-rank nondet entry under its old name (`main`,
`deterministic=False`) and its new name (`cake_gdn_nondet`). The test
ran at an earlier head on R200 (sm_107a) and on B200 (sm_100a). Each
platform gave `AB_RESULT EQUAL tensors_differ=0` over 4 shapes. GB300
and final-head results are TBD.
- **Each backend can be vendored and built outside `flashinfer`**
(#6553):
- No backend imports anything outside its own directory. The only
`flashinfer` import is a function-local `flashinfer.jit` import in the
shared `cake_build.py` template, used by the JIT route.
  - Neither KCP package imports its single-rank package.
- A copy of each nondet package, with every submodule, imports as a
top-level package while `sys.modules["flashinfer"]` is `None` (checked
on cluster CPU).
- The nondet KCP package recognizes the deterministic packed Q/K/V split
class by class name and module tail. Thus a vendored build keeps the
zero-copy gradient hand-off.
- **ALL_CAPS constants keep their names.** `DEFAULT_SCALE` stays in both
KCP facades and is not in `__all__`.
- **Metadata.** `pyproject` package-data keys,
`scripts/check_cake_build_manifests.py` rows and `.github/labeler.yml`
globs (`"flashinfer/cake_gdn_*.py"`,
`"flashinfer/experimental/cake/cake_gdn_*/**"`) use the new paths.
- **Shared package docstring.**
`flashinfer/experimental/cake/__init__.py` gets a docstring that
describes both modes. Backends named
`cake_<op>_<det|nondet>_train[_kcp]` live in this package. The docstring
says that the mode is part of the module name. It also says that no
entry point takes a `deterministic=` keyword. The module imports
nothing. The file is byte-identical in all #8928 family PRs, so those
PRs can merge in any order.

**Related issues.** This PR is part of #8928 and does not close it. Also
related: #8063 (non-deterministic GDN, closed). This PR follows #8920
and #8921, which are both merged. #8920 made the GDN KCP facade run only
the non-deterministic package (`deterministic=False` required). #8921
removed `flashinfer.gdn_train` and
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_train`. This PR branches from `main`
after both merges, so it carries neither change.

### Torch deterministic mode

In this table, "Torch deterministic mode" means
`torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`.

| Module | Torch deterministic mode off | Torch deterministic mode on |
|---|---|---|
| `flashinfer.cake_gdn_nondet_train[_kcp]` | Runs. Run-to-run bits are
not promised. | Runs unchanged: no alert, no warning, no fallback. |
| `flashinfer.cake_gdn_det_train[_kcp]` | Runs. Deterministic. | Runs
unchanged. Deterministic. |
<!-- VERIFY det row against the det facade docstrings at final head -->

The nondet entries run unchanged because every launch is fixed-order
today. The contract still does not promise run-to-run bits. A later
unordered launch would raise PyTorch's alert before it runs.

### Migration

Old module paths and names fail at import. There are no aliases.

**Former KCP facade.** Since #8920, the former facade
`flashinfer.cake_gdn_train_kcp` has run only the non-deterministic
package (with `deterministic=False`). In earlier releases, its default
`deterministic=True` ran the deterministic package. Callers that relied
on that default migrate to `flashinfer.cake_gdn_det_train_kcp`. Callers
that passed `deterministic=False` migrate to
`flashinfer.cake_gdn_nondet_train_kcp`.
